📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that many World of Warcraft: Forever players are presently in the midst of a substantial PvP reputation grind.
  • In a recent development, the battleground in question is Alterac Valley, a 40 person-a-side clash between Alliance and Horde factions, where both sides need to push their forces across a snowy, mountainous map into the opposing faction's base to take down the NPC General waiting there.
  • According to recent reports, played the intended way, Alterac Valley is a lengthy battle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that many World of Warcraft: Forever players are presently in the midst of a substantial PvP reputation grind. However, this process has been disrupted due to a sudden change to one of the game's battleground PvP arenas.

In a recent development, the battleground in question is Alterac Valley, a 40 person-a-side clash between Alliance and Horde factions, where both sides need to push their forces across a snowy, mountainous map into the opposing faction's base to take down the NPC General waiting there. Alterac Valley is being grinded by max-level players for its gear rewards that are given once reaching "exalted" reputation there. Currently it's some of the best gear available ahead of raids being introduced next month.

According to recent reports, played the intended way, Alterac Valley is a lengthy battle. The Generals on both sides are fearsomely tough but by rushing to capture certain structures on the way to this battle, you can weaken the Generals enough to make them easier to overcome. As such, players have been fast-tracking this PvP instance, skipping smaller objectives and rushing core objectives to get to the Generals as fast as possible. This bypassed a lot of the incidental skirmishing allure of Alterac Valley, but it was an efficient way to quickly gain reputation and Honor points (PvP currency).

But this strategy has been pretty much killed outright as of today. In a post made to the official World of Warcraft forums, community manager Kaivax revealed that the reputation gained from killing the Generals has been drastically reduced, while the reputation gained from killing other NPCs and capturing previously ignored objectives now grants more. Generals are also granted a buff that makes them incredibly strong for the first 20 minutes of a match, which is then reduced for each objective taken.

It has been revealed that this is a good change in regard to the experience of playing Alterac Valley. While rushing through was good for players looking to gain reputation swiftly, they weren't really playing the Battleground in the way it's meant to be played. The dev post reads: "The overall intent for all of these changes was for games to feel more meaningful while trying to maintain a similar amount of rep gained over a similar playtime within the battleground, even with longer match lengths. There will be fluctuations depending on how successful you are at destroying towers and holding capture points at the end of a match however.".

It has been revealed that so how has the community reacted? Badly! Taking a gander at community hubs following this change indicates plenty of frustration. Take this comment by Reddit user Athrek: "I'm fine with the changes if they give it Rank Points and calendar events. But they've gutted the rep for both sides, extended the time it takes to play, and it still gives zero Rank Points. Now you may as well get to the win condition and then sit there for a few hours, gaining the passive rep cause there's nothing else of value to be had.".

It has been revealed that it appears as of writing that the reputation gained isn't as much as it was previously, so those playing purely for reputation have been hit. There's another element of frustration which is that those who rushed to level 60 and ground Alterac Valley reputation and rewards before the changes won't be affected by this. Perhaps that's the allure of rushing to level 60!

Sources indicate that "This is why the WoW mantra is 'exploit early, exploit often'," writes user Lanienah12. "Some people are already exalted with AV rep and will receive no punishment for it; meanwhile new people will be spending 3x as long." Especially in the wake of the Blackmaw Hold gold exploit being discovered by these frontrunners, there's a growing belief that those taking their time or that are limited by real-life factors are feeling the brunt of these changes.

In a recent development, in August 2025, Aeternum Game Studios unveiled that Aeterna Lucis, the sequel to the well-liked 2021 metroidvania Aeterna Noctis, would be delayed from its planned launch in September of that year to sometime in 2026, for one good reason: Silksong. Just prior to that, Team Cherry surprised everyone by announcing that the Hollow Knight: Silksong launch was imminent, and Aeternum—and a whole bunch of others—decided the smart move was to just get out of the way.

Recent findings suggest that well, here we go again. Yesterday, Team Cherry announced that "Cherry Time" is coming on November 27, with "a bunch of exciting announcements, plus an upgrade on Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea of Sorrow," the Silksong expansion announced in December 2025. Some fans are hoping that means the Sea of Sorrow release date will be announced—or maybe even that it will actually be released.

Whatever's coming, Aeternum says that this time around, it's standing firm.

"Dear Team Cherry," Aeternum wrote in an Official Statement: Part 2 message, riffing on the "Official Statement" it put out in 2025. "A little over a year ago, just as we were about to launch our game, you announced Silksong. We stepped aside, pushed the whole project back a year, and, honestly, it was one of the best decisions we've ever made: The genre had an incredible year, and we got to enjoy Silksong as fans and polish Aeterna Lucis into the game we always dreamed it would be.

Recent findings suggest that "Now here we are again, just days from launch. Aeterna Lucis, our fresh Metroidvania, comes out on December 3... and you announce Cherry Time.

"This time we're staying put. Not to go against you, but because a lot of people have been waiting for the Queen of Light for a long time, and we don't want to make them wait any longer.".

Sources indicate that official statement, part II. Here we go again….

You might say that there's some element of opportunism at work here. Aeterna Lucis introduces on December 3, one week from today, and since that's surely way too close for another delay (not to mention it was pushed back a year already), the next-best option is to leverage this newly introduced Silksong moment in whatever way possible.

Aeterna Lucis and Hollow Knight: Silksong are both fantasy metroidvanias, and there's a lot of potential crossover there. "We have to ask, with all the love in the world: Is it just us, or does the universe have it in for us? Hahaha. And since you're about to wreck our lives all over again, the least we can do is make a bundle together.".

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Country music is so much more than an industry — it’s a community filled with supporters and cheerleaders.
  • Just look what happened when Us decided to celebrate Thanksgiving by asking artists to share a fellow musician they are grateful for this holiday season.
  • Time and time again, country singers shared stories of their peers who have offered encouragement, inspiration and friendship in times when it mattered most.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Country music is so much more than an industry — it’s a community filled with supporters and cheerleaders.

Need proof? Just look what happened when Us decided to celebrate Thanksgiving by asking artists to share a fellow musician they are grateful for this holiday season.

Time and time again, country singers shared stories of their peers who have offered encouragement, inspiration and friendship in times when it mattered most.

9-1-1: Nashville star LeAnn Rimes will never forget the opportunity she got to learn from Reba McEntire during a Dr. Pepper commercial.

As for Lady A’s Dave Haywood, he continues to look up to Tim McGraw for hitting all the right notes when it comes to “work-life balance.”.

Keep reading to see who your favorite country singers are grateful for this Turkey Day:.

I’m thankful for Dolly [Parton]. I am thankful for the light she shined on this world, for all the goodness, for her heart. There will never be anyone like Dolly, and I think she highlighted us what real heart looks like, and she radiated goodness. I just think we could all learn a thing or two from Dolly. I’m just grateful that we got to have her in all of our lives in this lifetime, and I’m grateful that I got to have the time with her that I did, and she was impactful and inspiring to me as not just an artist, but just as a woman in this world. And I always, like everyone else, I always think, “What would Dolly do?” And she would always meet everything and everyone with kindness.

It has been revealed that I’m thankful for my buddy, Thomas Rhett. I’ve known Thomas for a long time now, and I have always been a fan of the way he has approached music and his career while keeping his family first; I’ve always respected that. He’s been a role model to me not just in music, but in life. I love him to death and I’m proud to call him a friend.

It has been revealed that I would absolutely say Willie Nelson. He has had such a huge influence on me, being from Austin, that I just released a Willie Nelson tribute album. He is a true one of one, a legend, an amazing songwriter, and being on stage with him a few times has been a highlight of my career so far.

Recent findings suggest that I’d have to say Carrie Underwood! I remember early on, when I first got to Nashville, we swapped numbers, and I ended up calling her from the side of the road one day just to ask for advice. She was so gracious with her time and encouragement. She’s continued to be such a kind, steady source of encouragement over the years, even from afar. This industry can be a lot to navigate, especially when you’re young and figuring things out, so I’ve always been really grateful for the kindness she’s shown me. I grew up listening to her music and have looked up to her for a long time, so it’s been really special to experience that same kindness from her personally.

I would say Reba. She is one of the sweetest people I’ve ever known, and in my early, early years — and still to this day — if I see her, she’s just incredibly kind and supportive. I would definitely have to say she kind of tops my list. We did a Dr. Pepper commercial together in my early 2000s and she has always been someone who uplifts everyone around her, including myself. I just love her to death. I can’t say enough good things about her.

It has been revealed that I’ve always looked up to Hilary Duff, and she was actually my very first concert! Even though she grew up in the spotlight as a child star, she has always kept a strong head on her shoulders and remained true to herself. I love her message of ‘strong, not skinny’ and the way she continues to promote confidence, self-love and a healthy perspective on body image.

In a recent development, I’m thankful for Stevie Nicks. I’ve always been drawn to women who create an entire world around their music, and Stevie is the ultimate example. Her songs are romantic, haunting, feminine and fierce all at once. What inspires me most at this chapter in my life is how unapologetically herself she has remained. She reminds me that there’s power in your individuality, beauty in your scars and that a woman’s creative spirit only gets more interesting with time.

We are thankful for Jeffrey Steele. There’s something extra special about someone who believed in you back when you were just two guys chasing a dream. Jeffrey has been that person for us, mentoring us through the ups and downs of this industry. We wouldn’t be where we are today without him.

Recent findings suggest that I’m thankful for Tim McGraw and the example he has set for us as a band. His commitment to continuing his legacy through music and touring, while prioritizing his wife and three daughters, is such a beautiful picture of a successful work-life balance. He was actually one of the first to invite us out on a massive run, and hopping on his stadium tour this summer was something special. We also were so honored to surprise him during his induction into the Country Music Hall of Fame this year with our take on “Live Like You Were Dying.” He is so passionate about pouring into other artists, and having Tim be a mentor and friend all these years now means so much.

Recent findings suggest that I’m thankful to Vince Gill because he was the very first person who agreed to sing on my very first album, and I hadn’t even met him yet. This act of generosity has taught me to pay it forward with other artists or songwriters. He also told me that using wedges over in ear monitors allowed for the experience of being immersed in music fully. Nashville is the foundation for my songwriting. I’m so deeply grateful for this community.

Industry observers note that I’m thankful for Dolly because her talent and legacy have shown me so much. When I was 16, I convinced my parents to move me to Tennessee so I could sing in the country show at Dollywood. I guess you could say I’ve always been grateful for her!

I’m a country singer with California roots, so the west is in my DNA. The Bakersfield sound changed my world. It’s always felt like home to me, and Dwight Yoakam has carried that torch.

Sources indicate that before I had a record deal, Dwight took a chance on me and recorded “Heart Burn” with me. That duet changed my life. Singing with one of my musical heroes was a dream come true, and I’m just as grateful for the friendship that grew out of it with Dwight, his wife Emily, and their son Dalton. Dwight has become a mentor and someone I can call when I’m trying to make sense of this crazy industry. My favorite piece of advice from him is one I still carry with me. He told me, “Go with God.”.

Honestly, I’m thankful for Riley Green. There’s been a full-circle story behind our relationship that has shown me grace, humility and what it means to be a true friend. It revealed me that a true song wins. Songwriting is King and to treat others the way you wanna be treated.

Sources indicate that I’ve known and loved Sheryl Crow’s music since I was a kid. But over the past two years, while writing my last record and going through a deep season of transformation, I found my way back to her albums. Songs I’d known for years took on a completely fresh meaning. “Strong Enough,” “My Favorite Mistake,” “Maybe Angels,” “The First Cut Is the Deepest”. It felt like I was hearing them for the first time, with enough life behind me to understand them differently.

To me, Sheryl’s music is what embodied art sounds like. There’s something so instinctive about it, like the words and melodies could move straight from whatever she was feeling into the music. You hear the ache, the humor, the desire, the contradictions. It all gets to be there.

It has been revealed that in this season of my own life, I’ve been trying to remove as many filters as I can between myself and the audience. That’s made me appreciate the openness in her music even more. It reminds me how powerful a song can be when you let someone close enough to recognize themselves in you. I can get so caught up in finding the right words that sometimes I forget to trust the real ones.

I’m forever grateful for her songs, but just as grateful for her example: the dedication to her craft, the commitment to saying things that matter, and the courage to let the truest parts of herself find a place in the music.

In a recent development, this year, I had the privilege of opening for Kacey Musgraves on her Middle of Nowhere tour. After meeting her and getting to know her, it is clear to me why she is as successful as she is. Not only is she incredibly talented, but she pays attention to details and is very hands-on in everything she does. I witnessed her talking to the lighting director for an hour after her sound check until they got the colors exactly the way she wanted them. She works on all levels of her career. That is how it should be, and that is something I would like to apply to my own career.

According to recent reports, I’ll forever be thankful for my friend Keith Urban who was the first artist to take me out on the road as an opener. Watching him thrill crowds every night and run his entire tour like a well-oiled machine was a masterclass on how it’s done.

I’m thankful for Miranda Lambert because she has been supportive of me and my art from the beginning. She sends me long notes after binging my album, making me promise to keep going. She calls when she loves a song. When she asks how I’m doing, she genuinely means it. Miranda is as real and authentic as she is badass.

The fans! The way they show up for me and support me, it really inspires me to keep going and give them everything I have to give. I love The Lefties and I’m so grateful for them!

Sources indicate that I’m thankful for Deana Carter. “Strawberry Wine” was one of my favorite songs growing up. It reminded me of my high school sweetheart back in the day. It was just such a nostalgic country song, and it’s still so good even today. I remember when I first kind of started in the country world, I told my producer how much I loved Deana Carter, and she came over and we wrote a song together, and she let me sing “Strawberry Wine” with her, and she didn’t have to do that, and she’s so sweet and such a kind person. I still remember that. I wasn’t known at all in the country world, and she still took the time to sit with me, write a song and let me sing “Strawberry Wine” with her, and it was a memory I’ll always remember. I’ll never forget that.

Check our latest news in Google News.

Check our latest news in Apple News.

I’m thankful for Kristian Bush because he’s taught me to be bold, stay true to my roots and always enjoy the ride! A chance meeting at a songwriting festival in Hawaii turned into him producing my very first record, and now I’ve been out on the road opening for Sugarland on my very first arena tour! Getting to learn from one of my childhood heroes every night is a dream come true!

Sources indicate that I’m thankful for Rhett Akins because of the support, mentorship, friendship and opportunities he has given me. When I moved to Nashville, I had never done a cowrite in my life. Rhett took a chance on me, and we have now written multiple songs together, and I was also lucky enough to watch him be inducted as a member of the Grand Ole Opry this year.

I’m thankful for Russell Dickerson because he and his wife, Kailey, have been two of my closest friends for almost 20 years. I still can’t believe that writing songs with one of my best friends is a part of my job. We’ve been so lucky to celebrate some pretty big wins together, but getting to live life and raise our kids alongside each other is my favorite part.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Woot has dropped the price of the JBL PartyBox 330 to $479.95 for Black Friday, bringing it to its lowest price to date. For comparison, the same speaker right now costs $499.95 on Amazon's Black Friday sale, though that purchase includes a 90-day free trial of Amazon Music. Woot, meanwhile, offers free shipping for Prime members ($6 otherwise), and covers the newly introduced unit with a 90-day limited warranty.

Beyond the discount, the PartyBox 330 has plenty to offer if you're looking for a speaker that can handle everything from backyard barbecues to larger gatherings—sitting between the smaller Club 120 and the larger PartyBox 520 in JBL's lineup, it delivers deep, punchy bass and enough volume to entertain a crowd, while its roughly 20-hour battery life means you can keep the music going all day without having to find an outlet. It's also rated IPX4 for water resistance, so a little rain or an accidental splash shouldn't be a problem.

Recent findings suggest that that protection has limits, though—the 330 isn’t dustproof or particularly impact-resistant, so you’ll still want to be careful where you set it down. Audio-wise, sound quality also changes depending on where you're standing, with music becoming noticeably more muffled from the sides and behind. Fortunately, JBL's graphic equalizer and sound presets give you some control over the tuning. Its two microphone inputs and a guitar input also make it suitable for karaoke nights or live performances. You also get Bluetooth, USB-C audio, and an optical input for connecting it to a TV, along with Auracast support if you want to link it with other compatible JBL speakers for a larger setup.

Sources indicate that yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

It has been revealed that nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Recent findings suggest that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that ubisoft is clearly serious about implementing generative-AI deeply into the game development process.
  • That's according to a new Vertical Slice report, citing multiple anonymous sources at the moment working at Ubisoft.
  • In a recent development, several employees mentioned that pitching a game idea without gen-AI or without explaining why it does not involve the use of the controversial tech will not receive the greenlight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that ubisoft is clearly serious about implementing generative-AI deeply into the game development process. The French publisher now expects teams pitching fresh project ideas to be prepared to explain how gen-AI will help with developing the game.Teams who don't want to use gen-AI will need to clearly justify their reasoning to the higher-ups.

That's according to a new Vertical Slice report, citing multiple anonymous sources at the moment working at Ubisoft.

In a recent development, several employees mentioned that pitching a game idea without gen-AI or without explaining why it does not involve the use of the controversial tech will not receive the greenlight. This is especially relevant for smaller games with tight teams who now reportedly must deal with Ubisoft leaders' desire to implement gen-AI if they want to get their pitches reviewed.

Industry observers note that "We were told that using AI will increase the speed at which pitches can be made by 'small lean agile teams,'" one source mentioned. "We were told that as the goal was to move fast, iterate and discard projects to sift out the good stuff. AI was essential in maintaining a rapid pace.".

Recent findings suggest that while some mentioned Ubisoft is not openly mandating gen-AI use to staff, others feel "cornered" by gen-AI. One source said Ubisoft views the tech as "unavoidable", and that only a minority of the tech giant's audience reject it.

It has been revealed that ubisoft recently gave name to an internal initiative to expand the use of generative-AI and research how its developers can make use of the technology. It's called Motherbrain, and it has its own division within Ubisoft.

Over a year ago, Ubisoft embarked on a major restructuring effort that has seen the formation of new subsidiaries, the consolidation of its biggest brands into 'creative houses', the closure of studios and, of course, multiple rounds of layoffs.

"Ubisoft is in a top-down nightmare of AI psychosis," one source added, pointing to the already low morale within the organization. "Yves [Guillemot] has hitched his wagon to the tech, demanding the rest of the company follow on.".

NBC Is Aired Last Year’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, But Social Media Users Had A Way Better Idea

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I’ve got to be honest.
  • It’s still hard to believe that a Nor’easter came in and postponed the parade for the first time in its 100-year history (it has previously been outright canceled), and did so on the actual 100th anniversary.
  • It has been revealed that on Thanksgiving, NBC has opted to just throw on last year’s 99th Annual Macy’s Day Thanksgiving Parade at 8:30 a.m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I’ve got to be honest. I was NOT dreaming of a white Thanksgiving this week, but that’s what people in many parts of the country got. If you got up this morning wondering how to watch the 100th Annual Macy’s Day Thanksgiving Parade, you may have gotten a rude awakening: It’s not hitting the 2026 TV schedule until Saturday. NBC does have a Turkey Day solution, but honestly, it’s not the one people on the Internet want.

I’m right there with them. It’s still hard to believe that a Nor’easter came in and postponed the parade for the first time in its 100-year history (it has previously been outright canceled), and did so on the actual 100th anniversary. Not even from like, snow. It seems like strong winds made the whole balloon part of the parade impossible. That’s crazy bad luck. However, NBC isn’t sitting on its laurels (and neither is Jimmy Fallon). Here’s what’s happening.

It has been revealed that on Thanksgiving, NBC has opted to just throw on last year’s 99th Annual Macy’s Day Thanksgiving Parade at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones. NBC may have 99 problems, but no parade ain’t one. It’s not a bad idea really. The major balloons, c-list singers, and jazzy dance breaks are usually something most of us have on in the background anyway on this auspicious day. But social media users have a way better idea.

A slew of social media customers think the better play would be to throw on a really old Macy’s Day Parade instead of last year’s. One user on X put it perfectly:.

I don't know who needs to hear this, but there are full length recordings of Macy's Thanksgiving Day parades from the '90s, with all the commercials, on YouTube.

They later joked the lineup from 2003 “looked pretty good.” Another user had a specific year request, too, writing:.

If they were smart they would air one from, like, 1991 in full.

This isn't the first Macy's Day Parade controversy this season. If you'd rather go the nostalgia play, another X user even noted you can throw one of these old episodes on via YouTube, and I thank this individual for that hot tip.

Industry observers note that if you’re missing the Macys Thanksgiving Day Parade this morning you can find recordings of pretty much any year you want on YouTube. We pick a year and watch it every year mainly from the 90s before it turned into some weird rap event. 😂This year we are watching 1994.

It seems as if NBC’s strategy is the network doesn't want viewers to notice the parade is old, but there will be moments anyone actually paying attention to the broadcast should notice. I’m not saying that’s the world’s worst strategy given I already established a lot of us watch this while doing other tasks. Still, I think just going full in and putting on an older broadcast would be really fun, and I think would inspire people to pay closer attention and see what cultural references from the time are mentioned and what’s changed in the decades since.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Sources indicate that it’s a great idea, and now I just wish it was happening. Meanwhile, I’m still bummed I’ll have to wait a few more days to see Earl the Squirrel blown up in Epic proportion. Luckily, the Macy’s No-Longer-On-Thanksgiving Day Parade will make its triumphant return to NBC this Saturday. Happy 100th, y’all.

#211990. Fed up of Steam's lack of action regarding AI slop? Maybe you should take a look at the 'Games Without AI' event, instead

Fed up of Steam's lack of action regarding AI slop? Maybe you should take a look at the 'Games Without AI' event, instead

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that yesterday, a latest Steam event went live that claims all games featured in it have avoided AI entirely during development.
  • Sources indicate that "Behind every game, there are people, ideas, passion, and countless hours of creative work," mentioned a mission statement.
  • It has been revealed that there are plenty of games featured in the event, and not just ones tied to the organisers, as the cynical-minded amongst you may expect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that yesterday, a latest Steam event went live that claims all games featured in it have avoided AI entirely during development. The event, called 'Games Without AI', has been set up by a third party rather than Valve - by Dev Land Marketing, All Ages Of Geek, and Dark Cocooning - to "support real creators" and runs from 25th November to 6th December.

Sources indicate that "Behind every game, there are people, ideas, passion, and countless hours of creative work," mentioned a mission statement. "We've carefully curated a selection of independent games that celebrate human creativity, craftsmanship, and collaboration, all made without generative AI. But Games Without AI is more than a festival. It's also about bringing developers, players, and creators together to build a community where we share knowledge, support one another, and grow together.".

It has been revealed that there are plenty of games featured in the event, and not just ones tied to the organisers, as the cynical-minded amongst you may expect. Ones that jump out to my eye are: Pidgeon Pocket, a 'cozy incremental' with pixel art and a flock of adorable pigeons that you need to upgrade; Bottled by Bears, which tasks you with collecting and discovering rare bees, bottling honey jars, and expanding your farm; and Arctic Awakening, which sort-of looks like Pacific Drive meets Subnautica, in the Arctic.

Recent findings suggest that the event was posted to Reddit where commenters immidiately began accusing certain games of having used AI in their development - often without proof. One user, however, who claims to have been a developer trying to submit a game for inclusion in the event, offered some insight on how the selection process worked.

"As one of participants I can assure you that the qualification process was restrictive[ly] hard to bypass," they wrote. "We were all required to provide proofs of the game being made without AI and share as much of the process as possible. Then it was actually voted by community, which games are convicing enough so the whole process was intended to be as objective as possible. It's an event meant for developers who take pride in their games being made by humans so if any participant attends with ill intend of showing that AI generated game can get through... That would be very sad and shameful. From what I've seen, none of the selected games can be reasonable suspected of that. I also know some other participants personally and they are genuine zero-AI devs.".

It has been revealed that it's refreshing to see curation turned towards explicitly anti-AI games: between major publishers chasing the trend and smaller indie studios being caught out using the dubious tech, it's nice to see a library of games that promises that no AI was used during development. Given that Valve itself recently claimed it was up to developers themselves to ensure their games couldn't be ripped off by cheap AI tools, I'm happy to see an initiative rallying against the normalcy of all this.

Industry observers note that the most recent Steam Next Fest had more than double the number of demos than last year, but that stat isn't what it seems on the surface: roughly 17 percent of those games listed the use of generative AI, but it seemed that many more games did not disclose the use of AI in their development. In June's event, more than a thousand games in Steam Next Fest featured a generative AI disclosure of some kind, which made up roughly 20 percent of all featured games.

In a recent development, over the past 18 months or so, we've seen the glitch of generative AI in games on Steam evolve quite a lot. AI tools have been used to clone games, resulting in a troubling trend of imitation games taking the spotlight away from real indie devs. Whilst Steam, as a storefront, has been steadfast in requiring games to declare their use of generative AI during development, there are loopholes: devs that claim they only use AI tools for "efficiency gains" can appear on the store without any declaration.

At the other end of the spectrum is Epic Games' Tim Sweeney, who last year criticised Valve's requirement to disclose generative AI, saying, "Steam and all digital marketplaces need to drop the 'Made with AI' label. It doesn't matter any more." The swell of owners rejecting AI in games, though, seems to run counter to that argument. Recently, Big Walk developer House House revealed it used generative AI "sparingly" during the development of the co-op darling, and received a lot of backlash online.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re browsing home security options, Ring has one of the best Black Friday deals that should be on your radar. Right now, you can add an indoor camera and another one at your front door for less than $65. The Ring Indoor Cam 2K is 58% off at $24.99 (originally $59.99), while the Ring Battery Doorbell 2K is 60% off at $39.99 (originally $99.99)—both at their lowest-ever price.

Recent findings suggest that both offer features like 2K video and two-way talk, but the indoor cam is the simpler purchase if you mainly want to check on a pet or kids and see what’s happening near an entrance. It plugs into an outlet, so there’s no battery to recharge, and its low-light color video helps preserve detail when lights are off or dimmed. However, since it’s a fixed-view camera, keep in mind that you’ll need to position it carefully.

It also has a removable lens cover to block the camera’s view, which is a nice privacy perk, though closing the cover doesn’t turn off the microphone. For complete audio privacy, you need to disable the microphone in the Ring app.

The Battery Doorbell is the better pick if alerting you to visitors, deliveries, and potential intruders is your priority. It has a 140-degree horizontal and vertical field of view that provides head-to-toe framing, plus up to 6x zoom for better detail. You can install it without wiring, though you’ll need to recharge its built-in battery. It also requires a 2.4GHz wifi network.

The main catch with both devices is the ongoing subscription cost: Live viewing, two-way talk, and basic real-time notifications all work without a subscription, but reviewing saved footage requires a paid blueprint, starting at $4.99 per month or $49.99 annually for one device; coverage for multiple devices at one location starts at $9.99 monthly or $99.99 annually.

At these prices, the Ring Indoor Cam 2K is perfect for occasional live check-ins, while the Ring Battery Doorbell 2K is better suited to monitoring your front entrance. Buying both makes sense if you already have a Ring plan that covers extra devices.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Steam isn't running an official Black Friday fest—it indicates so right here in this revision, "Steam isn't running an official Black Friday fest"—but plenty of game developers have marked their stuff down to take advantage of the massive sale season, and so Valve is helping them all out a bit by "dressing up" its Discounts and Events page in the appropriate seasonal garb.

Is there a little bit of wink wink, nudge nudge to that 'not a Black Friday fest' business? Hey, maybe.

It has been revealed that in fair play, though, Steam traditionally hasn't run Black Friday sales, because its Autumn Sale was always happening at the same time. The realignment of seasonal sales in 2025 changed that, however, leaving a hole that was filled by the first-ever Steam Black Friday Sale last year.

Sources indicate that valve has other priorities this year, though, which could explain the absence (wink wink, nudge nudge) of an official Black Friday event on Steam in 2026. In September, Valve revealed changes to Steam's Discounts and Events page to make it prettier and more personalized, and it said in today's update that Black Friday is "the perfect time to share the updates we've been working on to make the Discounts & Events page a better experience altogether.".

With that all cleared up, I'll say that the Black Friday non-fest page is definitely an eye-catcher, and it will be interesting to see how Valve puts this section of Steam to work in the future. If it's treated like an 'almost a Steam sale' that never really ends, I have to think that developers and gamers alike will benefit—at least until we all get used to it and Valve has to figure out some upcoming way to tweak the formula.

For now, since we're here, let's check out some deals:.

Industry observers note that and here's one other difference between actual Steam sales and the Black Friday non-event: Valve noted the Black Friday decor will come off the Discounts and Events page on November 30, but the discounts themselves all have separate end dates. The Divinity: Original Sin 2 sale, for instance, also ends on November 30, but Outer Wilds will stay marked down until December 5, and the Esoteric Ebb deal will be valid until December 7.

#211986. Casting Director Francine Maisler on ‘Dune: Part Three’

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1920 w)

Casting Director Francine Maisler on ‘Dune: Part Three’

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1920 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch.
  • Recent findings suggest that luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival.
  • Recent findings suggest that when they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch. For the ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert’s 1965 sci-fi novel, they had to cast not only the lead character, Paul Atreides, but dozens of other main characters—powerful warriors, scheming royals, shape-shifting conspirators—to inhabit the world.

Recent findings suggest that luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival. “Denis’s vision is my compass,” Maisler tells Vanity Fair. “His passion [for Dune] since he was a teen was all I needed to follow.”.

Recent findings suggest that when they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film. “I did have an idea that they would have to have the presence and the acting talent to be able to carry this potentially for three movies,” she notes.

Sources indicate that dune (2021), starring Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides and Zendaya as Chani, was just the first step. Maisler returned to cast Dune: Part Two (2024), and Dune: Part Three, which will wrap up Villeneuve’s trilogy when it hits theaters on December 18.

Maisler is a titan of casting, having worked on hundreds of films with filmmakers such as Luca Guadagnino, Greta Gerwig, Aaron Sorkin, Paul Greengrass, Adam McKay, and Terrence Malick, and she was nominated for the first casting Oscar in 2026 for her work on Ryan Coogler’s Sinners.

Sources indicate that the casting Oscar didn’t exist when she began working on the Dune franchise, but this installment is likely to draw attention from the Academy. Over the three films, the cast has grown into an incredible ensemble, packed with many of today’s biggest movie stars, along with well-known veterans and a few unexpected choices. “One thing about Denis is if ever I bring him a name and he likes it, and I’ll say, ‘Well, do you want to hire that actor?’ He says to me something I think is so poetic,” says Maisler. “He says, ‘Francine, let me get back to you tomorrow. I need to dream about it.’”.

Ahead of the release of Dune: Part Three, Maisler looks back at casting the trilogy’s most important roles, including the exciting new additions to the upcoming film—and the possibility of more Dune in the future.

In Herbert’s book, Atreides is a slender 15-year-old with dark hair. “To find a 15-year-old who had that talent to carry this whole movie, we weren’t sure was out there,” remembers Maisler. The name that came up was then 22-year-old Chalamet, whom Maisler had previously cast in Hostiles, Beautiful Boy, The King, and Little Women. Chalamet, who didn’t have to audition but did meet with Villeneuve, would have to play Atreides from a young man who then begins to amass power in the second film and, after a 12-year time jump, is burdened with the choices he’s made waging a galactic war in the third. Though Chalamet hadn’t led a big blockbuster before, Maisler saw the depth of his talent. “I do think Beautiful Boy demonstrated me the depth of Timothée as an actor, as a young man, and that this was the next step in his progression as an actor, that he was able to hold a franchise in his hand,” says Maisler.

It has been revealed that there was a worldwide search for Chani, the skilled Fremen warrior from Arrakis who falls in love with Atreides. At the time, Zendaya was in the middle of filming the first season of Euphoria, and her graduation from Disney star to movie star had not yet happened. Zendaya screen tested with Chalamet, which sealed it for Maisler and Villeneuve. “She came in with five other incredibly talented actresses, but the minute you saw her with Timothée in a room, you just knew that there’s something special happening,” she claims. “She has such power when she walks in the room, and she’s breathtaking in the most interesting way.”.

Industry observers note that of course, Paul Atreides’s parents, Duke Leto Atreides and Lady Jessica, needed to look like Chalamet, but Maisler started with the characters’ essences when casting. Duke Leto Atreides was considered a fair and devoted leader as the noble head of House Atreides. Maisler saw that gravitas in Oscar Isaac. Lady Jessica becomes a force in the story because of her heightened physical and mental control as a trained member of the Bene Gesserit sisterhood. “Rebecca is so powerful, isn’t she?” claims Maisler. “She really, I have to say, surprised me. I always knew how talented she was, but she just owned that part.”.

Villeneuve and Maisler had worked with Brolin on the 2015 crime thriller Sicario. Maisler, who calls Brolin “one of our greatest actors,” was excited to have him back, this time playing Gurney Halleck, the Warmaster of House Atreides and a mentor to Paul Atreides. The character is described in the book as a warrior-poet, requiring strength and depth. “He’s so charismatic, so masculine,” notes Maisler of Brolin. “He’s kind of a throwback from other generations.”.

When Momoa’s agent brought up Momoa’s name, Maisler wasn’t quite sure about the idea because at the time he was known for starring in the DC movie franchise as Aquaman. “I was a bit skeptical, I have to admit, because I knew he had this incredible presence on screen, but I didn’t know, truly, his talent, and that’s taught me a lot about being open to people who come from different types of films,” she says. Villeneuve was more open to the idea at the start, and met with him about playing Duncan Idaho, a fierce fighter and protector of Paul Atreides. He returns in the third movie as a ghola—a sort of clone—named Hayt, which demands a more complicated performance from Momoa. “Jason’s an incredible artist, and I’ve come to just love him,” says Maisler. “He’s so funny. I want to put him in a romantic comedy next, because he really is one of the big surprises in the ensemble.”.

Industry observers note that taylor-Joy had already risen in stardom by the time she joined the franchise for the second film. Her breakout was in The Witch, and she starred in hit series The Queen's Gambit, which earned her a Golden Globe and a SAG Award. This made it slightly surprising that Alia Atreides, Paul’s volatile sister, makes a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it appearance in the second film. “I give her a lot of credit for not counting lines in the second one,” says Maisler, who says Taylor-Joy signed on for the second because of the potential of the third installment. Indeed, in Dune: Part Three, Alia is a loyal sister and vengeful force who is not afraid to get blood on her hands. Taylor-Joy’s charisma and intensity will jump off the screen, says Maisler. “Actors are very smart, and they know when to trust a director like Denis,” she says. “When he says there is going to be something in the third film and he describes it, he will make it happen.”.

It has been revealed that A tribal leader of the desert-dwelling Fremen, Stilgar is a seasoned warrior and becomes a devout follower of Paul Atreides as Muad’Dib. The role required a level of intensity. “Oh, I think we all just prayed that Javier would do it,” says Maisler. “I think every actor wants to work with Javier, and he’s one of probably a handful of actors I think can do anything.”.

According to recent reports, pugh joined for the second film as well, but like Taylor-Joy, she didn’t have a ton to do. But Princess Irulan, who marries Paul Atreides as a political union, is a key part of the plot in Dune: Part Three, joining a conspiracy against Paul. Maisler first saw Pugh in the 2016 film Lady Macbeth, and then cast her as Amy March in Gerwig’s Little Women. “You saw on that what an intelligent actress she is, and singular,” she says. “She knows no boundaries, and she’s confident and bold.” She says Pugh has always reminded her of Debra Winger, the star of An Officer and a Gentleman (1982), and Terms of Endearment (1983). “She’s just commanding, and she has this energy, and everything she does is fascinating,” says Maisler. “You can’t take your eyes off of her.”.

Sources indicate that the third installment brings in yet another major star with Pattinson, who plays Scytale, a shape-shifter who is conspiring to dethrone Paul Atreides. Maisler, who also worked with Pattinson in Primetime, which also came out this year, describes him as “one of the versatile actors in his choices.” She had also worked with Pattinson on Mickey 17, which proved that he could play many different versions of a character—a skill that would be required of him in this third Dune movie. “Robert's a tremendous actor, and I think he takes these really bold chances,” notes Maisler. As for his recent announcement as the next James Bond, Maisler has faith he and Villeneuve will deliver. “I think the way Denis and Rob created the character in Dune: Part Three together speaks to the surprises that we will see in Bond,” she says.

For Dune: Part Three, Maisler and Villeneuve had to find two actors who looked like twins and also looked like the offspring of Chalamet and Zendaya. They initially hoped to cast real twins, but didn’t find the right pair. In the end, they found their Ghanima and Leto II in Ida Brooke and Nakoa-Wolf Momoa. Brooke, who looks strikingly like Zendaya, is a relative newcomer who previously appeared on Apple’s sci-fi drama Silo (which stars Rebecca Ferguson). And Nakoa-Wolf Momoa, who makes his feature acting debut in Dune: Part Three, is Jason Momoa’s son—though Maisler didn’t know that when she first watched his audition tape. “Then came this tape of this young man who had incredible presence, and—we didn’t ask for this—he added some combat footage to his tape,” she says. Maisler says sometimes actors will call in a favor to get their child an audition, but Wolf, as she calls him, got this on his own. This casting was the most crucial for the third film because of what might be to come. “It was almost like casting the first one where these two young actors could go on to potentially, if there’s another movie where they’re leads,” says Maisler. There have been no official announcements of any future Dune movies, but for those mourning the end of the Villeneuve trilogy, Maisler is planting a small seed of hope here. The third Dune book, Children of Dune, centers on Leto and Ghanima, which means the two young actors Maisler found may have more story ahead of them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Team Ninja is known, in part, for developing difficult games, but producers Kohei Shibata and Masakazu Hirayama emphasized during an interview with INVEN Global at GCON 2026 in South Korea that thereâs a key difference between difficult and unfair. The pair also spoke about how the Koei Tecmo subsidiary approaches the use of AI in games development, and an awkward compromise between implementing the technology for repetitive QA tasks, while arguing that “what matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands.”.

Shibata and Hirayama are best known for their work as producers on the Nioh and Wo Long series respectively, two games that take the combat-driven difficulty of the iconic Ninja Gaiden franchise and transpose it onto the world of samurai and Chinese mythology. Before the topic of AI arose, the two discussed the crucial role of player interaction and movement in their games, beginning with the similarities between all three franchises and most notably their swordplay and the focus on timing your attacks and reading an opponentâs next move. According to both, this process of requiring a player to learn an enemyâs next move and counter is key to straddling the line between challenging and frustrating play.

âI consider Nioh to be samurai action,â explained Shibata. âSamurai combat involves stillness and movement. You stand firmly grounded, observing the opponent’s moves, and deliver a sharp strike the instant an opening appears.â Meanwhile, for Hirayama on Wo Long, that game was defined by âaggressive Chinese martial arts action,â where âattack and defense flow together seamlesslyâ and where âaggressively attacking is vital, but defense must also lead directly into the next attack.â.

Industry observers note that the two go on to argue that it’s notable to make a game that is polished in a way that reduces friction between a player’s action and consequence. If a person fails, it must be their fault, not the game’s. âI believe [the core essence of action games is] control responsiveness,â Shibata explained. âWhen a player presses a button, the character must move exactly as they intended. If you press a button and the character doesn’t react properly, it causes frustration. Conversely, if a slight input causes an exaggerated movement, it feels awkward. Therefore, responsiveness to input must be simple and intuitive, and the movement must be communicated rapidly.â.

We have seen numerous studios speak out in recent times about where they will and wonât use AI. While some Japanese developers are embracing the technology, others are more cautious, either avoiding it entirely or insisting they only use the technology for optimizing their development framework while leaving creative choices to humans. The latter is the direction being taken by Capcom with its next generation of RE Engine, and appears to also be the choice being made by Team Ninja, who are already using AI for QA purposes.

In a recent development, as Shibata explained, âCurrently, we utilize AI in QA and various verification tasks to streamline certain workflows. If we can use AI to shorten task times, we can dedicate that saved time toward elevating the game’s overall quality. In that sense, using AI is beneficial. However, since it is still a new technology, we are continuously evaluating the most appropriate ways to implement it. I imagine other game companies are facing similar questions.” He continued,.

What matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands. Repetitive, simple tasks that anyone must perform can be streamlined using technology. But ultimately, deciding how to craft the game and what makes it enjoyable must be done by humans. Using AI itself should never become the goal. I believe the principle that humans must think for themselves and finish the game will remain unchanged in the future.

Sources indicate that where, if anywhere, is an acceptable use of AI is a topic that remains up for debate, but it appears many developers are settling into a space where it is used to handle repetitive tasks. The use of AI in QA actually predates the modern conversations of generative AI, and doesnât necessarily rely on the tech: Sony, for instance, has been experimenting with AI for many years to test games. Whether this is something audiences are willing to tolerate, or indeed is something that will further threaten jobs in the games industry, remains to be seen.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 75-inch Hisense U6SF Pro has dropped to $747.97 from $1,399.99 for Black Friday sale—bringing it to its lowest price to date. The rest of the U6 Pro lineup is discounted as well, so you can pick up the same TV in sizes from 55 inches to a massive 100 inches, for anyone with the room for something closer to a home-theater-sized screen. Whichever size you choose, you’ll get free delivery to the room of choice—a service that normally costs $19.99. As for the TV itself, it’s a 2026 model that sits below the U7SG (also on sale for $1,297.99, from $1,999.99) in Hisense's lineup as the brand's entry point into Mini LED, pairing a 4K panel and local dimming with a matte, anti-reflective coating meant to cut down on glare, notes this PCMag review.

Industry observers note that for a budget set, the U6 Pro gets a lot right when it comes to picture quality—its high peak brightness helps it hold up during a sunny afternoon in a living room with big windows, so a daytime football game or cooking show won’t look washed out, while its excellent contrast and effective local dimming keep dark scenes looking deep when you settle in for a movie at night. It also does a good job cleaning up lower-quality content, which is useful for older cable broadcasts or compressed YouTube videos—and its Fire TV interface makes it easy to jump between those kinds of content and the major streaming services without needing a separate streaming device.

Recent findings suggest that the U6 Pro also brings plenty to the table for gaming, with HDMI 2.1, VRR, ALLM, and a 144Hz refresh rate that PC gamers can push to 240Hz at a lower 1080p resolution. That said, the panel’s slow response time and poor motion performance can reportedly make fast-moving scenes look noticeably blurry. Viewing angles are limited too, with the picture losing quality fairly promptly when you move off-center—and its built-in speakers aren’t particularly impressive either, so a soundbar could be worth budgeting for.

Åkerman jokingly agreed that things would be easier for them with some men out of the way.

For most of Survivor 51, I thought the season’s defining trait was going to be its wacky and over the top characters. We had a professional wrestler cutting off his thumb. I could go on and on about all the vibrant personalities, but with only two episodes to go in the season, it’s now becoming clear Survivor 51 might be best remembered for something else: producing one of the most dominant winners ever.

There are seven castaways left on Survivor 51, and Sharonda is both the best connected player and the one who seems to be running the entire game. Fans have been all over her as the likely winner of the season for weeks, but this past episode in particular screamed her credentials from a helicopter in Fiji. She was given credit in very specific detail for engineering both of the last two votes, and as viewers, we’ve been told exactly where she stands with all the key players left in the game. I mean seriously, let’s just run down her relationships that have been spelled out explicitly.

Recent findings suggest that she’s in a secret pact with Jelly and Devin as part of the helicopter alliance. As an audience, we have been told about this secret group since the first episode, but the remaining players still have no idea what’s going on. That alliance is clearly the main story of the season, and she is right at the center of it.

Then there’s Cristian, who we have seen Sharonda repeatedly manipulate. First he told her about Carter’s idol, then she lied and convinced him to turn on Maggie. It was only at the end of this past episode, after he watched Carter walk out the door, that he finally realized she’s not his friend. Then there’s Eric, who she straight up remarked she can get to do whatever she wants. I have to assume he feels the same way since he got no confessionals this week to rebut that.

It has been revealed that we saw some tension between her and Mike this week, as she advocated for Carter being eliminated and he advocated for Thien An being eliminated. I bet you can guess who won that massive showdown. Carter went home, and Mike ultimately voted with Sharonda, despite the fact that he had a final two alliance with the loveable farmer. Maybe he’ll give us a confessional next week where he explains why he went down that path, but from the perspective of the audience, it looks like she just barrelled over him and got her way.

In a recent development, ordinarily, when Survivor indicates us a player looking this dominant this early in the game, it’s a bad sign. It means everyone else is about to conspire to get them out because they’re such an obvious threat to win the game that they have to be eliminated. Maybe that’s what we’ll see with Sharonda, but I’m not so sure that’s going to happen this season. We’re not getting confessionals from other players about how she needs to be taken out, and there aren’t actually many people left in the game who the edit is telling us can win.

In a recent development, seriously, who else can win this game right now? Jelly is definitely the other most likely contender. She’s gotten a main character edit, and we’ve heard castaways talk about how she’s a threat to win the game, but she got two total confessionals this past episode and players have repeatedly talked about getting her out during their confessionals. Devin still has an outside shot I guess. He’s this season’s leader in confessionals, but the edit has also repeatedly dunked on him for all the mistakes he has made.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Sources indicate that that goes double for Mike. We’ve gotten his perspective pretty consistently, but we’ve also heard a ton from other players about how much they don’t like him. He's possible but very, very unlikely. Eric is a wacky side character who seems like a zero vote finalist. Cristian had two confessionals in the first four episodes combined and Thien An is the most underedited player in the entire season who we’re repeatedly told has no allies. Those are the players who are left.

Industry observers note that I’m not saying Sharonda is for sure going to win Survivor 51, but if she does win Survivor 51, she is probably going to be remembered as one of the most dominant winners ever. She hasn’t had a single vote cast against her, and she’s voted correctly in every single tribal council so far, except the one where Linnea went home and multiple advantages were played. I’m not counting the Devin and Jelly vote because she’s the one who told them to play the idol and then told us, as an audience, very explicitly that she only voted against them so the rest of the tribe wouldn’t know she engineered the entire thing.

Industry observers note that that's actually a positive for her, as is the fact that she’s formed the best relationships with the largest group of players. She also won an individual immunity idol and has gotten basically zero negative content from the edit. Seriously, what are her bad moments? I'll wait...

If Sharonda wins, it is going to look dominant, and we’re going to be talking about her in the same way we do Tony, Kim and other legends who gave us a masterclass. There’s still a long way to go, but at this point, I think it’s better than 50-50 it happens.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that more about convenience than chasing top speeds, you can use the Roam 7 as a standard router, connect it to public wifi to create a private network, or share your phone's internet through USB tethering.
  • Once it’s running, the hardware covers the basics, with a 2.5 Gbps port for a wired connection like a hotel’s Ethernet jack, a 1 Gbps port for a wired device, and a USB 3.0 port for a storage drive or phone tethering.

A novel solution for connecting to the internet on the go, the TP-Link Roam 7 travel router is now down to $83.49 from $119.99 for Black Friday, marking its lowest price to date. This isn't a full-size home router but, as the name suggests, a compact travel companion that measures roughly the size of a paperback book, with foldable antennas that let it slip easily into a bag.

Recent findings suggest that more about convenience than chasing top speeds, you can use the Roam 7 as a standard router, connect it to public wifi to create a private network, or share your phone's internet through USB tethering. It also supports Ethernet input and USB modems, along with range extender and wireless client modes. That flexibility is particularly useful when you’re juggling a laptop, phone, and maybe a tablet and would prefer not to sign each one into a shaky network separately. Setup is straightforward through the TP-Link Tether app: scan a QR code, choose your connection type, and you’re online in a few minutes.

Once it’s running, the hardware covers the basics, with a 2.5 Gbps port for a wired connection like a hotel’s Ethernet jack, a 1 Gbps port for a wired device, and a USB 3.0 port for a storage drive or phone tethering. And since it draws power over USB-C (5V/3A), a basic power bank can keep it going through a long layover or a camping trip. As handy as it is on the road, though, it’s not meant to replace a full-size home router—even with its 5 GHz band and Wi-Fi 7 support—which will generally offer better coverage and more consistent speeds. Real-world performance also depends heavily on your connection and setup. USB tethering, for example, can feel slower than using your phone directly. It also leaves out features like automatic band steering, so you may end up managing networks yourself. Still, if you travel often or need a portable network hub for multiple devices, you’ll find it holds up pretty well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new survey of Grand Theft Auto 6 players has found some particularly interesting results. 30 percent came away from the game with the desire to buy someone special flowers. Nine percent punched cats.

Per Games User Research's director Steve Bromley, 303 players from across the UK and US were polled on their experiences. They had to have at least two hours of playtime to contribute, which led to an informed sample of how folks are finding the game.

Sources indicate that those polled gave the game an 8.4/10 (that's 4.2/5 Eurogamer readers), which is glowing praise. 42 percent loved the narrative, as well as Jason and Lucia's relationship. 38 dug the lifelike and believable world, while 35 percent were keen on the freedom to explore and the variety of activities.

As for what they didn't like, 28 percent weren't a fan of the slow pacing and long cutscenes, 19 percent didn't like the difficulty in stealing cars and losing a wanted level, while 18 percent were put off by the game's technical performance.

Now for some fun findings: 41 percent expressed an interest in improving their real life after playing the game, with 30 percent of those looking to buy a loved one some flowers. Nice! 14 percent were at least once confused or stuck, due to confusion with the stealth, identifying time-sensitive missions, or experiencing control challenges.

According to recent reports, there's some bad news for the cats out there, too. Nine percent accidentally punched a cat while trying to pet it, while 61 percent had the same experience with human NPCs. At least it wasn't intentional, that has to count for something. Right?

When Kate Middleton stepped out on the green carpet at the Earthshot Awards ceremony in Mumbai this week, it was “an absolute princess moment,” says British designer Amanda Wakeley.

“Catherine has really come into her own. She has found her stride and a newly introduced confidence, and you see that in this dazzling but also practical ‘tourdrobe,’’’ Wakeley, who has previously dressed the Princess of Wales and used to dress Princess Diana, tells Vanity Fair.

Industry observers note that it has been 10 years since Princess Kate last visited India. Her fashion choices are more sophisticated now than on her visit in 2016, and the speech she delivered at the Earthshot Prize ceremony on November 17 shows a upcoming confidence. With her elevated look, there’s no trace of High Street labels. Kate’s flared floral dresses and the wedge shoes she used to love (but the late Queen Elizabeth apparently disliked) have been replaced by Manolo Blahnik pumps, couture power suits, and clothes by some of her favorite designers, such as Emilia Wickstead.

Prince William and Princess Kate attend The Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

Kate’s decision to wear a striking vermilion dress made from handwoven silk by Fresh Delhi–based designer Mahima Mahajan to the Earthshot Prize ceremony spoke volumes. The eye-catching dress, which she paired with a burgundy Prada velvet clutch, was chosen after Kate had selected a special suite of emeralds from the royal gem collection. The green stones on the dress perfectly matched her jewels, which served as an homage to both Queen Elizabeth II and India, as the green of the Indian flag represents growth and prosperity.

Sources indicate that the dazzling stones known as the “emerald tassel suite” were worn frequently by the late Queen Elizabeth II, and while Kate has previously worn the earrings, this marked the first time she wore the set. The effect was dramatic.

“Never has Catherine looked more like a queen in waiting,” Wakeley says of the look.

Recent findings suggest that wearing the suite ensured that Kate, who has free rein of the royal jewels, looked more regal than ever. “What was fascinating was seeing Catherine wear these incredible family heirlooms along with more relaxed collections from some of her favorite modern jewelry designers like Kiki McDonough and Astley Clarke,” remarks Wakeley.

Kate’s carefully curated wardrobe for the trip wasn’t just about power dressing—it was also about showing she can be sustainable as well as on trend.

“It was good to see Catherine making a proper nod to sustainability by rewearing her Roksanda dress,” Wakeley notes. “It’s clear a lot of thought has gone into her outfit choices. Her wardrobe has to be practical, and her clothes have to work harder than most people consider for their clothing; she needs weight in the hem of the floaty dresses. She has learned lessons the hard way. She is often seen bending down, talking to children, so she’s conscious of how low a neckline is, how short a skirt is.”.

Princess Kate visits the Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital, on November 18, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

For her visit to Mumbai’s Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital on November 18, Catherine chose a striking red tailored Emilia Wickstead skirt suit with Manolo Blahnik pumps. On November 16, she opted for a pistachio blazer by designer Veronica Beard, paired with white Alexander McQueen trousers and pearl-buckled Camilla Elphick flats, a relaxed and accessible look for when she picked up a cricket bat.

Princess Kate plays cricket on November 16, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

It has been revealed that as Princess of Wales, Catherine is often compared to Princess Diana. “The main difference is Diana was a fashion icon. Catherine has become a style icon,” Wakeley states. “There’s a massive difference. Diana played into the fashion of the day and was finding her style. During the time she resigned from public life, she worked out her style DNA. Catherine has had to do that on the job. Very wisely, she has worked out her style and doesn’t get too impacted by fashion and trends. She goes for what she likes. What works for her rather than trends. She really knows now what works for her.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Luke Wilson reflected on the legacy of The Family Stone in the midst of shooting next year’s highly-anticipated sequel.

Industry observers note that “I feel like I’ve just kind of been in a bubble making it here for the last month,” Wilson, 55, exclusively told Us via his partnership with Fanatics. “It was one of those movies where, you know, it was really fun to make the first one. A great group of people. It came out and people seemed to like it. But then it was a few years later, I’d start to hear things like, ‘Oh my family and I watch that every Thanksgiving,’ or ‘My family and I watch that every Christmas.’ Each year it seemed like more.”.

It has been revealed that the actor added, “I’m so used to Chevy Chase and Christmas Vacation or It’s a Wonderful Life. So when people started to say their families were watching The Family Stone, I remarked, ‘Really?’ But now it does seem like it’s become a genuine tradition for people.”.

In a recent development, the Family Stone was released in 2005, featuring an ensemble cast including Rachel McAdams, Dermot Mulroney, Sarah Jessica Parker, Claire Danes, Craig T. Nelson and the late Diane Keaton. A sequel was announced in September with all of the original cast set to return, plus the addition of 9-time Emmy winner, Jean Smart.

“I’m wary of saying anything about the damn plot because I feel like I’d have the studio come down on my head,” Wilson joked. “I’ll just say people get together, people split apart, babies are born. It revolves around Christmas again and I think it comes out in November of next year.”.

Wilson plays Ben Stone — sibling of Everett (Mulroney), Amy (McAdams), Susannah (Elizabeth Reaser) and Thad (Ty Giordano) — who ultimately ends up with Meredith (Parker) at the end of the first movie.

While Wilson was understandably coy about what to expect from the sequel itself, he gushed about the experience of reuniting with the cast.

“I’ve never gone back to the same characters, the same group of people,” Wilson explained. “It’s been really fun. Just to be around Sarah Jessica, who was so great to work with. She kind of helped put the movie together.”.

He added, “It’s been great to be around Craig T. Nelson. He’s been really funny. He’ll just be like, ‘What are we doing, man? Why are we here? Why am I here?’ But it’s been a good feeling.”.

In addition to returning to The Family Stone, Wilson is the face of Fanatics’ Town Hall, the brand’s season-long NFL campaign. The campaign features Wilson alongside former NFL great Calvin Johnson and former LSU gymnast and influencer Livvy Dunne, celebrating the passion of NFL fans and highlighting FanCash, Fanatics’ universal rewards currency.

He added, “It’s just fun to be around those guys. They just seem like superheroes.”.

It has been revealed that while tech can get pretty expensive, especially in our current "RAMageddon" era, there are still plenty of affordable devices out there. The problem, of course, isn't quantity, but quality: Buying a tech item for under $50 is risky, since many of these products are made as cheaply as possible. If you're looking for a portable Bluetooth speaker, for instance, you don't want to buy something with poor sound quality, or that doesn't easily connect to your devices, or that breaks unexpectedly.

You don't need to worry about any of that with the JBL Go 4. This is a solid portable speaker that just so happens to have an MSRP of $49.95. It's so good, I named it Lifehacker's best gift under $50, as its price, excellent sound quality, and feature set make it a great option for most anyone on your list. It's an even better buy during Black Friday, too: Right now, you can pick up the JBL Go 4 for as low as $31.95, 36% off the original retail price.

JBL's Go 4 is a small speaker, but it gets surprisingly loud—especially for a speaker at this price point. Like other JBL speakers, it places a particular emphasis on bass. This is a tiny speaker, so don't expect a subwoofer on the go, but not only will it let you hear the bass in your music, it is noticeably punchy. JBL advertises seven hours of playtime on a single charge here, which is often plenty for taking the speaker out and about for the day. You can net an additional two hours of if you engage "Playtime Boost." JBL doesn't specify how this works, but it likely cuts some of the frequencies here to save on battery life. And, since it's 1P67-rated against dust and water, it's a great choice for outdoor use.

Recent findings suggest that perhaps my favorite thing about the JBL Go 4 is that it supports Auracast. That means you can easily connect to any other Auracast-compatible JBL speaker using the Auracast button on each device. I've used this before at parties and gatherings for an impromptu multi-speaker setup. Since JBL is so popular, it's not impractical to assume one or two other people at the function might have a similar speaker you can connect to, or if you know friends or family members have JBL speakers of their own, you can coordinate these setups ahead of time.

It has been revealed that this discount is only available on specific colors of the Go 4, at least on Amazon: Black, White, Blue, Purple, Red, and "Squad." Black and Orange, Pink, and Sand are all still $49.95. Again, the JBL Go 4 is absolutely worth the $50 MSRP, but unless you're married to one of those three colors, it's even better at a discount.

Industry observers note that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

#211970. We are already in a world where people think about promoting games as human-made, Citizen Sleeper creator notes
