📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jana Kramer is reminding divorced parents that it’s OK to feel a variety of emotions as they navigate the holidays with or without their kids.

“I think it’s hard because no matter what, it’s not normal for a mom to wake up on Christmas and not have their kids,” Kramer, 42, exclusively shared with Us before the release of her new Lifetime holiday movie, Love on the Christmas List. “This is the year that I don’t get to see my kids on Christmas morning, and I don’t know which is worse. I don’t know whether it’s worse to not have them in the morning or to say bye to them on Christmas Day.”.

Kramer shares daughter Jolie, 10, and son Jace, 7, with ex-husband Mike Caussin. She also welcomed son Roman in November 2023 with husband Allan Russell.

It has been revealed that “Last year was the first year that I didn’t have a full, complete meltdown. I just kind of had a little cry,” Kramer continued. “I don’t beat myself up for that anymore because I just think about how it’s not supposed to be a normal thing. I’m a mom who wants her kids every day, and I want to wake up to them running down the stairs on Christmas morning. And this year, I don’t get that.”.

The former One Tree Hill actress finds comfort in knowing her two oldest kids have a nice time at Caussin’s house. As many parents can relate to, however, Kramer wishes her time wasn’t cut short.

“I do know that they’re having a beautiful morning at their dad’s, and I’ll be ready to open the door for them and have a great rest of the day with them at noon on,” she noted. “But I think for any divorced parent that splits on Christmas Day, you dread the morning of not having them, or you dread the noon on Christmas Day having to say goodbye. And to this day, I don’t know which one’s worse.”.

Instead of “doomsdaying it,” Kramer has vowed to make the most of the time she does have with her kids. She’s also filled with gratitude for the healthy relationship she has with Caussin, 39, after their public divorce in 2021.

Industry observers note that “I think it’s progress on both or all of our ends, you know,” she said. “But you just want your kids to be happy, and you know that they are. That’s the win right there.”.

Before Santa arrives for Christmas, Kramer is celebrating Thanksgiving with plenty of food, family and gratitude.

This holiday season, the actress stars in a new Lifetime movie Love on the Christmas List, which is part of It’s a Wonderful Lifetime.

“I would say this is very similar to all the moms that are on the hunt for the best toy for their kids,” Kramer teased about the film. “For this movie, it’s about whether you do what you need to do, whether it’s for your job or for your child, and in the middle of that, you might find a little romance along the way.”.

That love interest may just be actor Ignacyo Matynia, who plays a widowed dad also on a quest to find a special gift for his daughter.

“He’s wonderful. He’s great,” Kramer noted of her costar. “I’ve never met him before, but he’s such a good actor. We had a lot of fun together.”.

With the holiday movie season officially underway, the host of iHeartRadio’s “Whine Down” podcast is grateful that her movies are part of so many family celebrations. She’s also happy to be in a place to experience the magic all around her.

In a recent development, “I think for a long time, I’ve felt unsteady and just like an anxious heart, and I just feel like my children are happy and healthy right now,” she told Us. “I’m healthy, I’m happy. I’ve got a beautiful little family, and I’m really grateful for that because I know that there are a lot of people going through a lot of things, and whether it’s with health or sad hearts, and I just feel for the first time, I feel a very peaceful heart, and that makes me happy.”.

Love on the Christmas List premieres on Lifetime Saturday, December 19, at 8 p.m. ET.

The Thursday Night Football matchup on November 19, the day that GTA 6 came out, had the lowest viewership of the entire season so far for a TNF game, but the low ratings might not be due entirely to competition with GTA 6. The data reveals that 12.23 million people, on average, watched the November 19 matchup between the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans on Prime Video. That was a 9% slide from the Week 11 Thursday Night Football matchup in 2025 featuring the Latest England Patriots and New York Jets. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dJDf76QVv70 Looking at week-over-week, the November 12 matchup this year between the Washington Commanders and New York Giants drew 16.27 million viewers, and was up 17% compared to the Week 10 matchup in 2025 featuring the Las Vegas Raiders and Denver Broncos. Due to the poor ratings of the November 19 TNF game, the full-season average now for TNF games this season sank to 16.62 million on per game. One expert told GameSpot that live sports like football probably won't be too heavily impacted by GTA 6 because people want to watch in real time. The low ratings for the November 19 matchup could be partially attributable to competition with GTA 6, but a likelier scenario is that people tuned out because it was a boring game in which the heavily favored Texans throttled the Colts by a score of 26-3. The Texans were up 17-3 at the half, and the game only had nine more points total scored in the second half--all by the Texans. Not exactly thrilling stuff that people would stay glued to. Ahead of GTA 6's launch, people also wondered how The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which released on November 20, might be impacted. It may have been, but the film still put up massive numbers at the box office that exceeded expectations. GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies via pre-purchases alone and generated close to $4 billion on day one. The game will continue to sell, and it should get another jolt of sales when the PC edition arrives in 2027, as rumored. Sources indicate that this trailer properly spooked me! It’s superbly well put together, compiled from the found footage of a missing cinema employee.Â Late Shift is about exploring and spotting anomalies in a looping reality that evokes Backrooms-like creepypastas, but showing clear and welcome influences from Control as well. Its mix of art styles, impossible architecture and jumpy nature feel really evocative to me. Can’t wait.

Developer: TMA Games Release Date: Out now (Early Access) Steam.

Torment Hexus had me at “kicking CEOs out of windows.” It also had me at combining match-3 spellcasting alongside a tactical roguelite combat grid. What I’m communicating is that it has me. Now, at least: this entered Early Access in August this year, and intends to emerge fully-formed by some point in 2027. It’s presently playable, “pretty smooth and polished,” they say, but there are prepares to add many more bosses, fresh spells, and a major ol’ story to justify multiple runs through the intriguing concept.

Developer: Mullet Games Release Date: 2027 Steam.

Industry observers note that building a city in the desert is hard enough, what with the lack of water and basic resources, but what about the massive sandstorms blowing in and burying your settlement in sand? That’s the setup forÂ Storm Settlers (a name I struggle to see how Ubisoft will allow, given the genre overlap with itsÂ Settlers franchise), a super-cute and challenging city-builder. To survive your little guys will have to dig down in the hope of discovering the water table, while also building up defenses against the ceaseless storms that sweep over your town. The game is having a public playtest in December.

Developer: Pixelnest Studio Release Date: Q1 2027 Steam.

Industry observers note that one of my favorite phenomenon is watching as rudimentary gaming genres cross over and develop complexity, as if driven by the same forces that cause evolution to keep pointing things toward becoming crabs.Â Cosmo Cargo is a great example of this, merging the trend for inventory management games with the trend for auto-battlers, and creating a space-exploration game with hireable crews, hostile enemies, and battles based on the synergies created by the way you’ve combined cargo in your inventory. There’s a demo, of course, and the game is out next year.

Developer: ElSchorscho Release Date: December 2 Steam.

In a recent development, I have a real soft spot for the dumbest incremental games, with their moreish progression and self-effacing inherent nonsense, and Drunk Woodcutter perfectly fits that bill. Due out next week, the short game is about chopping logs with increasingly silly tools…while getting drunk. This leads to hacking at logs with a banjo, and making money in the process, and as such reflects all our lives.

Developer: Lost Token Release Date: Out now Steam.

Theropods is a traditional point-and-click adventure, but with the twist of containing no words or dialog at all. You play as a young cave women living with a tribe, haunted by dreams of the gruesome death of her mother in the mouth of a dinosaur. Yup, it’s a dinos and cavemen living together story! TakeÂ that, evolution. Now an adult, she needs to get on with the caveperson life, be it hunting, mending pots, or saving her people from the terrifying attack of marauding enemies, raging fires, and alien artifacts falling from the sky. Doing this with no words at all makes for a simpler game, but an intriguing one, boosted by some utterly stunning old-school pixel art animations.

Developer: Speldosa Interactive Release Date: Dec 7 Steam.

A third-person platformer crossed withÂ PowerWash?! Yes please! That’sÂ Muri: Wildwoods where you play as an adorable mousey cleaning up and restoring an island to make it all lovely. To get around, it’s third-person jumping and climbing, and there are even watergun-based puzzles to solve. Powerwashing with double-jump is something I didn’t know I needed, but now it’s all-consuming. Thankfully there’s only a couple of weeks to wait until it’s out!

Subscriptions to streaming services can add up swiftly, especially as companies continue to regularly raise prices. But most streamers also offer discounts for Black Friday, so if you've been holding off on signing up for a upcoming service or returning to one you've canceled, now is the best time of year to audit your subscriptions and take advantage of deals.

HBO's Black Friday deal drops the price of a Basic subscription to $5.49 per month for 12 months (normally $10.99 per month). This tier is ad-supported and doesn't include live sports, but the deal is available as a standalone subscription, a Prime Video add-on, and through Roku.

Peacock's ad-supported Select plan typically costs $8.99 per month or $89.99 per year, but the service's Black Friday promo brings it down to $2.99 per month (for three months) or $29.99 for an annual plan. The ad-free Premium subscription is at the moment discounted to $8.99 per month for three months or $89.99 for one year (normally $12.99 per month or $129.99 per year).

Beyond the major players, there are plenty of other streaming deals for Black Friday.

Recent findings suggest that many services are heavily discounted as Prime Video add-ons, including MGM+, Starz, AMC+, and Crunchyroll. Roku has similar subscription deals.

Starz is also offering standalone discounts on its monthly blueprint ($2.99 per month for three months, down from $11.99 per month) and its annual subscription ($11.99 for year, down from $69.99).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I watched my first season of Dancing with the Stars this year, and the journey has definitely been a doozy.
  • There was a ton of discourse about DWTS during its last few episodes, with pro Sharna Burgess slamming how fan votes factor in.
  • The rest of the internet, totally different story right now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I watched my first season of Dancing with the Stars this year, and the journey has definitely been a doozy. After tuning in to the competition show on ABC, I was shaken up by the twists and turns that came, including the power of the fan vote that resulted in both Jenna Dewan and Harry Shum Jr. being eliminated ahead of the finale. It turns out that finalist Connor Wood joked about being portrayed as a villain prior to Ezra Frech's historic win.

There was a ton of discourse about DWTS during its last few episodes, with pro Sharna Burgess slamming how fan votes factor in. Plenty of folks online were mad about Wood staying on, while (what many felt were) superior dancers like Harry and Jenna got eliminated. During an interview with THR prior to the finale, Connor spoke about the fan perception of him, offering:.

The rest of the internet, totally different story right now. We’ve gotten to a point where I have become a bit of a villain for some people.

In a recent development, obviously, Connor didn't do anything actually villainous, but his getting through to the Dancing with the Stars finale was a shock for many viewers out there, especially when you compared his performances to those of other contestants. His placement seemed to be entirely due to fan votes, since Wood had the lowest scores in the final weeks of the show. Some fans were worried about whether or not underdog Tatyana Ali would stay in the competition, which ended up resulting in Connor becoming the "villain" of the seasons.

Sources indicate that clearly, the fan vote on Dancing with the Stars is notable, but it can also seemingly create more division and drama for those watching the acclaimed reality TV series. Later in the same interview, Wood spoke more about this perception as a contestant, offering:.

In a recent development, I think that they think that I personally voted their favorite off, and it’s like — I’m aware of my level of dance skill. I have nothing to do with me staying here. That’s just been just the dark side of making it as far as we made it. My understanding is that the more that people go home, the more the fans of those people will go to someone else’s page and villainize those people. That’s sad, and it’s just a testament to how invested people are in this show.

In the end, Connor would end up in third place on Dancing with the Stars Season 35, beating fellow finalists Maura Higgins and Tatyana Ali. I can only imagine how his "villain" persona might have been amplified if he managed to place even better... especially if he ended up beating Ezra as the winner taking home the Mirrorball trophy this season.

Ultimately the final two pairs of the season were Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov, as well as Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach. The latter would end up going home with the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy, following a viral final performance where the paralympic athlete's prosthetic leg came off mid-performance. It was a truly epic moment, especially when he managed to overcome it and finish the final dance with his partner.

I thought Ezra was deserving of a win before this final dance, but after seeing the way he overcame and finished the performance, the idea of Connor somehow beating both him and Amber was cringeworthy. In the end that didn't happen, and hopefully Wood can shake off his villain status as more time passes.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Dancing with the Stars is streaming in its entirety for those with a Disney+ subscription as part of the 2026 TV schedule. We'll just have to see what drama comes with the next season of the wildly popular series.

  • Industry observers note that not even porn is immune to the GTA 6 effect, as it's just one of several forms of entertainment that has seen a decline in viewership since the massive open-world game launched.

  • Industry observers note that according to Mashable, US traffic on Pornhub--which I've been told is one of the largest pornography websites, by traffic--dipped by as much as 15.5% an hour after GTA 6 launched.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that not even porn is immune to the GTA 6 effect, as it's just one of several forms of entertainment that has seen a decline in viewership since the massive open-world game launched. It's not surprising, given the game's record-breaking start, with 32.5 million sales from preorders alone. On PS5, GTA 6 is the "biggest launch" in PlayStation history, and players spent an average of 17.4 hours playing in its first few days--which probably didn't leave much time for a quick browse of after-hours material. According to Mashable, US traffic on Pornhub--which I've been told is one of the largest pornography websites, by traffic--dipped by as much as 15.5% an hour after GTA 6 launched. Paradoxically, Pornhub traffic had actually been up by 16.5% compared to average days, likely indicating that people were bored and randy. Pornhub traffic started to fluctuate after the GTA 6 launch and reached an average peak a few days later. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i7l7Lu69V_c Thanks to the game's massive success, we're also seeing the Rule 34 effect on GTA 6, as Mashable's research noted a 16,196% spike in GTA-related searches. Up to 15 million search queries were made on November 18 alone, with customers searching for GTA 6, the GTA 6 strip club, and content depicting the co-protagonist Lucia specifically. The fan-favorite stalker--and possible serial killer--Mandy also appeared in search results, while Lucia's partner-in-crime Jason ranked low. Thursday Night Football also saw a big dip last week, with the lowest viewership of the season so far for a TNF game. While Rockstar's upcoming open-world adventure can't be blamed entirely for that dip, it certainly must have had an impact, given that the football game was held on GTA 6's launch day. That effect didn't extend to the box office, as The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened to a massive $120 million in the US, almost triple that of the last film in the series, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes. For more GTA 6 news, you can read up on how modders are attempting to make an unofficial PC port, how to fix GTA 6's broken HDR, and you can check out our list of walkthroughs in the GTA 6 guides hub.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that EA is ditching seasonal updates and shaving some of the live service fluff off Skate (for some reason stylised as skate.) going forward.
  • "EA and Full Circle are committed to keep driving skate.
  • Skate's fifth and final season is coming to an end on 1st December, with Full Circle embracing a different model from there on out.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that EA is ditching seasonal updates and shaving some of the live service fluff off Skate (for some reason stylised as skate.) going forward. Normally, such news would be cause for concern. Here, the publisher assured players the transition will lead to more regular updates since devs can now push out new features without waiting for the next season to roll around.

"EA and Full Circle are committed to keep driving skate. forward. Just as a reminder, we're still very much in Early Access," the studio wrote in a new blog post. "The game is still a work in progress, and we're using this valuable time to experiment, iterate, and figure out what works best for the long-term health of the game - especially when it comes to social features and progression. Ultimately, we want to build skate. in a way that lets us roll out fresh content much faster, even if it's not totally finished yet.".

Skate's fifth and final season is coming to an end on 1st December, with Full Circle embracing a different model from there on out. "We are transitioning away from the traditional seasonal cadence in favor of regular, agile content updates," it explained.

Recent findings suggest that full Circle is also throwing out the skating sim's version of a seasonal battle pass (horribly named skate.Pass) by the end of the year, and will rethink how the game's progression system works: "We've mentioned it many times: we have a long-term future vision for skate, and this is a key part of it. Update 0.33.1 will be our very first update in this post-season era.".

Sources indicate that the move away from rigid seasonal updates "gives the development team the freedom to launch features earlier in their lifecycle," the blog post continued. "This means we can deploy work-in-progress mechanics and gather your direct feedback to continuously shape and build upon San Vansterdam. We've started this with in-game testing of features such as Spot Battles, Block Parties, and Prox Chat before rolling it out officially, and we’re going to continue with this process.".

Sources indicate that full Circle's live service rejig also means the in-game currency Tix is being retired, and some maps will no longer be locked behind paywalls. Skate still has real-money microtransactions and a cosmetics store, though it's nice to see some of the more aggressive live service bits being plucked out.

The Challenge alum Nicole Zanatta welcomed twin daughters Seraphina and Madyson on May 1. “Becoming their mom has been the greatest blessing of my life, but our journey hasn’t been easy,” Zanatta wrote via Instagram on June 1. “Both of my girls were diagnosed with congenital CMV (Cytomegalovirus), a virus I had never heard of until it became part of our story.” She continued, “Since birth, we’ve spent time in the NICU, attended countless appointments which are still ongoing, undergone testing and started medications. I recently brought them home a week ago, but our journey is far from over. Through every high and low, I choose faith over fear, resilience over doubt, and gratitude for every blessing along the way. I will give my girls every opportunity to thrive. I will always fight for them and advocate for their needs.” According to the Mayo Clinic, CMV is "a condition caused by a common virus.” The CMV virus stays in the body for life once a person is infected and can spread through body fluids, including blood, saliva, urine, semen and breast milk.

#211928. Tech Report: GTA 6 Is A Tragedy Because You Cannot Sit Down And Eat Spaghetti

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1427 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Kotaku ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: GTA 6 Is A Tragedy Because You Cannot Sit Down And Eat Spaghetti

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1427 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Kotaku

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Everyone, including me, has been making much (rightfully) of how incredible the level of detail in GTA VI is.
  • In a recent development, you cannot sit down and enjoy a slow, relaxing meal.
  • I love cooking through video game cookbooks, I love beautifully designed and rendered meals within game worlds, and I love creative food crafting systems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6Grand Theft Auto VI.

Everyone, including me, has been making much (rightfully) of how incredible the level of detail in GTA VI is. This game is ridiculous, man! The sheer amount of incidental and specific dialogue, the clothing, the way characters move, the weather, the TV and radio programs, I could go on all day. But there’s a single aspect I’ve found where the level of detail genuinely felt short of what I’d hoped for going in: the food.

In a recent development, you cannot sit down and enjoy a slow, relaxing meal. There is nowhere to order a plate of spaghetti or other food to be eaten explicitly there, in the establishment. There is no cooking. There is only fast food and takeout. And that’s how I know this game is going to be a tragedy.

I love video game food. I love cooking through video game cookbooks, I love beautifully designed and rendered meals within game worlds, and I love creative food crafting systems. So I’m always on the lookout for such things! And in one respect, I actually think GTA VIÂ does food beautifully. It isÂ freaking incredible that you can hold a food and a drink (or two foods, or two drinks) in each hand simultaneously, and swap between consuming each of them at will. Last night, I took Lucia out to a food truck and bought an empanada and a mojito. I had her stand there and take bites of the empanada, and watched with wonder as the empanada disappeared, bite by bite in her hand. (I tried to take a sip of the mojito but accidentally pulled my gun instead and someone called the cops, but I’m sure it would have been equally impressive).

Recent findings suggest that much has been made of this system, and deservedly. Jason takes bites of apples, and the apples having those bites visible in them until only the core is left! The pair will drink liquids, and you can see the liquids in the containers slowly recede! All of these items have unique models, too: burgers, tacos, croissants, the grilled fish sandwiches made in an early mission that have different levels of char as Jason cooks them…God, it’s incredible! Hats off!

According to recent reports, I don’t want anything about that system to change. I love being able to eat handheld foods like this. But what bothers me is that this is…all that Jason and Lucia ever eat.

I complained about this earlier, after a glimpse in the pair’s fridge in an early trailer. Mostly alcohol and protein shakes. Nothing substantial whatsoever to keep two active crime-doers properly fed. But at the time, I thought that was just…their state at that moment in the game. I assumed eventually the pair would end up in a situation where they ate food like normal human beings.

Yet this never happens. I’m in chapter 3, and I’ve consulted with our reviewer who has finished the game, and my understanding is that the pair will never evolve beyond eating on the go. You can’t order a plate of spaghetti or some lo mein and sit comfortably and lazily consume it. The pair never cooks food at home, either as a mechanic or even as a visual suggestion, as their cabinets remain full of nothing but plain bread and cereal and unused pots and pans right up until the end of the game. Every restaurant that looks like it could be a proper sit-down dining establishment is closed and locked to you, and everything that’s open serves like, five things: water, soda, beer, and roughly two handheld food items. And those same 10-20 food items are repeated ad nauesum across all the game’s restaurants, regardless of what’s on the posted menu. In a small handful of establishments, you can sit down to eat those items, but it still doesn’t look like the two are relaxing over a meal. Again, I understood this early in the gameâthe two were broke, Jason was living a bachelor life, and they were on the run. Hell, the motel room in Chapter 2 doesn’t even have its own coffee pot. I get it.

Sources indicate that but as the two move to Vice City, build wealth, and start living at a higher standard, I really just thought there’d be some option, somewhere, for one of them to take the other out on a nice dinner date. Maybe just a little cutscene showing a decent plate of food with the two all dolled up. Or perhaps, if that was too risky, the barest suggestion that either of them had ever cooked at home: TV trays, or a dirty pot in the sink, or more than like four spices sitting in the window for some reason. Even like, aÂ discussion about having eaten a meal?

So on one level, I’m disappointed. I love seeing gorgeous food renders in games, and I can only imagine Rockstar’s would be stellar. I think a lot about how the Dragon’s Dogma team bought expensive steak just so they could film themselves cooking it for the game. Or the absurd feasting scenes in Monster Hunter with gorgeous cheese naan. Or even the very simple scenes in the Yakuza games, where you couldn’t see the food, but you could hear the characters discussing how it tasted and what their thoughts were. Impressive as the handheld food is, I’m not really excited at making Jason eat another croissant after I’ve seen the animation a few times. He doesn’t talk about it, it doesn’t seem to do anything for him, he doesn’t even really seem to derive any pleasure from it. Just a health boost maybe.

But even as I’m disappointed by all the storefronts I can’t enter and the menus I read but can never get Jason or Lucia to order from and eat, I’m starting to get what GTA VI is trying to say here. It’s not a budget or a time matter, I know that. If Rockstar devs had wanted to make gorgeous food or record discussions about eating it, they would have. I really do think GTA VI wants to convey in every possible way that this pair will never, ever be safe. They will not be able to slow down or stop or rest for the kind of luxurious meal I want them to have. And that’s luxury not even just in terms of spending lots of money on nice food, but the luxury of time and safety: spending the time to sit, in public, and eat it regardless of where that is. The kind of luxury I feel when my husband and I go to our favorite local Indian joint and, instead of ordering takeout, sit and eat out of the metal trays and sip chai and share naan. If Jason and Lucia sit to eat at all, it will always be in chairs that are easily pushed out, in empty greasy spoons where they can make a quick getaway.

According to recent reports, I suspect that wherever the story is going, it is not going to a place where they will be able to comfortably enjoy a slow glass of wine and a fine risotto. It’s not even that it’s an option I can see on the horizon, out of reach due to price or other limitations. It is just, permanently and forever, not for them. Maybe I’ll be proven wrong, and there will be a perfect, peaceful, happy ending where the pair get to live a normal life with their son in a safe place with minimal crime, and where they can go out for a massive plate of spaghetti that all three can sit down to enjoy over a wonderful hour of laughter and merriment. Maybe there’s a world where someone could reasonably imagine the three enjoying a multi-hour, homecooked Thanksgiving together. But given all the crime I’ve been doing, somehow I feel that a happy and normal future will, like the many, many restaurants of Leonida, be forever closed to them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as part of CD Projekt's latest earnings report, the Polish developer revealed latest information about its projects and headcount. For the quarter that ended on October 31, The Witcher 4 was the company's biggest project by headcount, with 513 people working on it. That's down from 519 people for the quarter that ended on July 31. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=54dabgZJ5YA&rco=1 For comparison, the number of developers on Cyberpunk 2 rose from 184 to 199 and staffers on the new IP codenamed Hadar jumped from 33 to 34. The codename Sirius game, believed to be a multiplayer The Witcher game, saw its development staff shrink from 84 to 60; the project has undergone numerous shifts throughout its development as CD Projekt reworks the experience. CD Projekt's total development headcount rose from 1,045 to 1,051. CD Projekt's overall development headcount rose to 1,051 people. In terms of money, CD Projekt reported Q3 revenue of 208 million PLN ($51 million USD) and net earnings of 109 million PLN ($26.8 million). CD Projekt spent a lot--more than 177 million PLN ($43.5 million) on development costs during the quarter--but the company's total cash reserves grew by 31 million PLN ($7.6 million USD). CD Projekt has a number of big projects in the works, including The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past in 2027 and The Witcher 4 in 2028. Cyberpunk 2 is also on the way, but it doesn't have a release window yet. The company is also working on a game with Scopely, the mobile gaming giant owned by Saudi Arabia. Cyberpunk 2 was in the news recently, as the game's creative director joked that the RPG is now canceled because GTA 6 is so good.

#211926. Sell Thy Neighbor: Trump Official Howard Lutnick and the Clandestine Deal to Sell NYC’s Glamorous Pierre Hotel

Sell Thy Neighbor: Trump Official Howard Lutnick and the Clandestine Deal to Sell NYC’s Glamorous Pierre Hotel

📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5691 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that here it was, the major reveal.
  • Sources indicate that about 42 seconds after it started, things went off the rails.
  • The setting was the Cotillion Ballroom, the chandeliered 4,000-square-foot event space at Newly introduced York’s iconic Pierre Hotel, the site of Al Pacino’s blind tango in Scent of a Woman, where the ceilings are 19 feet high, the curtains are golden, and the windows offer views of Central Park’s southeast corner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that here it was, the major reveal. After years of planning and wrangling, after more than $10 million spent on engineers and lawyers and architects, after all of the rumors and headlines and finger-pointing, the long-awaited presentation was ready to be made.

Sources indicate that about 42 seconds after it started, things went off the rails. A “shitshow,” as multiple people would later describe to Vanity Fair the two-and-a-half-hour meeting on the morning of July 29.

The setting was the Cotillion Ballroom, the chandeliered 4,000-square-foot event space at Newly introduced York’s iconic Pierre Hotel, the site of Al Pacino’s blind tango in Scent of a Woman, where the ceilings are 19 feet high, the curtains are golden, and the windows offer views of Central Park’s southeast corner. Seated at round tables were 40 or so of the people with enough disposable income to call the Pierre home, or at least a home: investor Austin Hearst; Tory Burch, the fashion powerhouse; Lois Chiles, the 1970s-era movie star and model. Joining remotely was Michael Eisner, the former Disney CEO, who last year spent $4.3 million to buy a second apartment there and, with it, even more shares in the co-op that owns the Pierre.

Sources indicate that in came representatives from the Khashoggi Holding Organization out of Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, and the Dorchester Collection, the luxury hotel management firm owned by the Sultan of Brunei. Their proposition was straightforward. Khashoggi wanted to buy the Pierre—the nearly 200-room hotel and all of the apartments too—for $2 billion, less expenses. It was an enormous haul, even for a neighborhood this tony. And it would be all in cash. “The funds are presently available,” a Khashoggi representative promised.

But if the residents with two thirds of the co-op’s shares accepted the offer, everyone would have to move out. Neighbors would be voting, in effect, to force their fellow neighbors from their apartments.

It would be in their best interest, the Dorchester and Khashoggi reps stated. The Pierre was a gem, but a tarnished one after 96 summers and thousands of guests. It didn’t have many of the amenities that come standard these days in a five-star hotel. The façade was already undergoing a $22 million overhaul, and there were deeper, systemic problems to solve. The CEO of the company managing the Pierre publicly complained it was something of a money pit. All of that would change after Khashoggi bought the place, the presenters promised. Dorchester would invest more than $1 billion into the Pierre, giving the landmark building a grand upcoming entrance on 61st Street, a pool in the basement, and structural renovations throughout.

When it was done, the residents would be first in line to buy apartments at the all-fresh, all-modern Dorchester-managed Pierre, ready to last another century.

According to recent reports, the response in the Cotillion room was instant and not particularly friendly. Some residents had moved in not long ago. Others had spent millions remodeling their apartments. “How are we going to enjoy all the perks of this wonderfully renewed building when we’re forced to sell at a price you determine and we have to buy reconfigured apartments, not our own, at market prices?” asked Tina Beriro, the philanthropist and longtime resident, in a recording of the meeting reviewed by Vanity Fair. Like many of the residents, Beriro, at 85, was only a few years younger than the hotel itself. “Many of us are going to be dead by the time you finish.”.

Christopher Cowdray, Dorchester’s white-haired, Zimbabwe-born president, didn’t have an answer. Nor did he provide much of a response when asked what would happen to the more than 400 people who work at the hotel. “In this case, we are still in discussion at the moment,” Cowdray said, to audible groans.

It has been revealed that “Many employees have worked here 30 and 40 years and are just about to hit retirement,” Burch pointed out, per the recording. “I have people in the elevator crying that they feel like their job is on the line.”.

The questions kept coming. For years, shareholders had begged—and even sued—to find out more about the sale. But the long-promised detailed plans for the Pierre’s purchase were still weeks away, adding to the tension in the Cotillion room. (One source, very much in favor of a sale, later called the decision to make an elaborate presentation to the shareholders without those specifics “idiotic.”).

“Look, ladies and gentlemen, I’ve been on the board of the Hearst Corporation for over 25 years. Sat on the boards of many corporations, for profit and not for profit. I have never seen anything like this,” Hearst said, his voice cracking. “This is a serious problem that you have presented to the shareholders, and you guys have done a miserable fucking job.”.

According to recent reports, one of the many lawyers in the room interrupted him, and they started going at it. Cowdray and the other presenters were escorted out. At one point, the wife of Michael Stern, the 88-year-old chairman of the co-op’s board, tried to offer his resignation on his behalf (which he then turned down). Even by the famously hostile standards of New York City’s high-end co-ops, this was nasty.

Recent findings suggest that ironically, the co-op’s biggest shareholder—the resident with the most at stake in the sale financially—didn’t show up. Howard Lutnick was busy in the Oval Office that day with President Donald Trump in his role as US commerce secretary.

Lutnick had bought the Pierre’s 16-room penthouse, its largest apartment, in 2017 for $44 million. If the sale of the Pierre were to go through, Lutnick would get as much as $100 million for the penthouse, even as his neighbors were forced to sell and hundreds of hotel staffers’ jobs were put in jeopardy. Newmark Group—the real estate services firm hired by the Pierre’s board and controlled by Cantor Fitzgerald, the brokerage house previously run by Lutnick—would earn tens of millions more.

Newmark may have a reputation for shepherding substantial-ticket sales to completion. But in a letter to the Pierre’s board last year, Beriro called the hiring of the Lutnick-linked firm “a blatant conflict of interest,” an allegation sources close to Lutnick and the board deny. One Pierre resident tells me that Lutnick’s involvement is symbolic of a “culture of corruption” that extends from 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue in Washington to the edges of Central Park in New York. Others imply it is part of a different pattern: the purchase of more and more of America’s most valuable assets by companies and sovereign wealth funds from the Persian Gulf’s petrostates, at times orchestrated by those in and around the second Trump administration. Those shareholders wonder whether Lutnick had personally worked behind the scenes to maneuver the Khashoggi group into place to buy the Pierre, and that speculation spilled onto the pages of The New York Times.

BALL GAMES Guests attend a Valentino party in the Cotillion Ballroom at the Pierre hotel, 1970, Newly introduced York.

In a recent development, A source close to Lutnick notes that he formally cut ties with Newmark in early 2025 and adds that, since his move to government, Lutnick’s only involvement in the Pierre sales process has been to respond to media reports like this one. A spokesperson for Sabre Park Avenue LLC, Khashoggi’s American holding manufacturer, tells Vanity Fair in a statement that “any insinuation or implication that the proposal, the transaction or the parties involved engaged in improper or undisclosed conduct is categorically false.”.

I spoke to more than 15 sources and reviewed hundreds of pages of documents related to the Pierre deal, including previously unreported text messages between Lutnick and Khashoggi and a corporate intelligence dossier dropped in my mailbox.

Turns out, the shareholders were right to wonder about Lutnick’s role.

Recent findings suggest that the Pierre for decades was synonymous with Upcoming York glamour. At the height of their star power, Audrey Hepburn stayed in the hotel’s suites and Elizabeth Taylor kept an apartment there. The restaurant’s original menu was created by Escoffier. Barbara Walters had a reception for her final wedding at the Pierre (about 10 years after she and my grandfather, the Broadway producer Lee Guber, officially split). Yves Saint Laurent owned a two-bedroom on the 38th floor, which was later bought by Valentino cofounder Giancarlo Giammetti, who then sold it to former Bottega Veneta creative director Tomas Maier.

In a recent development, and yet for 15 years or more, there’s been a growing sense that the Pierre’s best days are behind it, even as the stars continue to use the hotel to get ready for the Met Gala. A 2010 Wall Street Journal article mentions how the Pierre “lost its glory.” By the time Lutnick swooped in to buy the penthouse in 2017, he did so at an $81 million discount off its original asking price.

THE TORY PARTY Fashion designer Tory Burch, in one of the hotel’s elevators, was among the residents opposed to the sale.

Industry observers note that since then, age has continued to take its toll. Scaffolding has surrounded the hotel since at least 2018, according to city records. Exit a multimillion-dollar apartment with a spectacular view of the park and you’re liable to find worn carpets or hallways with the faint odor of mold. Rooms at the Pierre tend to cost much less than they do at the Plaza or the Ritz-Carlton, just around the corner.

Industry observers note that over time, a group of shareholders became particularly vexed with Taj Hotels, which had managed the property since 2005. There were complaints of broken elevators, empty concierge desks, and “slipshod maintenance.” Maier, in an October 2023 co-op-wide email, lamented that Taj delayed long-planned renovations to his apartment for months, citing high hotel occupancy. (A Taj spokesperson said in a statement those concerns “reflected a specific point in time rather than the overall trajectory of the property.”).

Recent findings suggest that what Maier may not have known—and what the residents I spoke to were unaware of—was that the Pierre’s board had already explored the possibility of replacing Taj. The only way to do that, to break the contract with Taj, was to sell the Pierre. In April 2023, the board drafted a memorandum of understanding with the Maybourne Hotel Group, which is primarily owned by members of the Qatari royal family, to buy the hotel portion of the Pierre. “But there was a condition,” a source familiar with the matter tells me. “Everybody had to move out for two years.” The source adds, “You cannot renovate a 100-year-old building with people living in it, right?”.

Sources indicate that that was a deal killer. So the board decided, in this source’s words, to hire a firm that could broker a “more acceptable” sale. They picked the real estate consultancy Newmark. Lutnick was still chairman of Newmark’s board at that time, though two sources say he had no role in the decision. (The board, through its attorney, declined to comment for this story. But a Newmark spokesperson says its “unanimous” selection was “based on the firm’s experience advising on some of Fresh York City’s most complex and high-profile real estate transactions.”).

Industry observers note that from there, “Newmark went out to find another buyer,” the first source adds. Its fee at the time: $50,000 per month, to be counted against any future commissions in the event of a sale. (Eventually that was bargained down to a flat $30 million.) The board retained the high-profile law firm Fried Frank, which had represented Lutnick’s companies before, to assist Newmark in its search.

LONDON'S CALLING Christopher Cowdray, the Dorchester Collection’s president, was part of the contentious presentation to residents in the Cotillion ballroom at the Pierre.

Sources indicate that since Lutnick’s financial firm, Cantor Fitzgerald, owned a controlling stake in Newmark, that gave Lutnick an incentive to see the Pierre sold. He had another: According to the source connected to Lutnick, his 12,000-square-foot penthouse triplex had been uninhabitable since 2021, when a storm had caused catastrophic damage. Lutnick concluded, according to the source close to him, that major repairs wouldn’t make sense if they weren’t accompanied by a larger round of structural renovations to the building. In the meantime, he installed a basketball court in the apartment to make some use of the place.

When the sales process started, the idea was to make a deal for the hotel only. The upcoming owner would likely want to consolidate guest rooms on certain floors. That meant some Pierre residents might be encouraged—strongly encouraged—to sell, but not necessarily everyone.

Sources indicate that brokers approached everyone from Mark Zuckerberg to Michael Dell to the king of Morocco to buy the place. Most of the residents were in the dark. As far as they knew, Newmark was trying to help renovate the building, not sell it off. Nor did they know Lutnick was personally trying to wrangle potential buyers for the Pierre.

On Wednesday, May 8, 2024, Lutnick’s private jet took off from Teterboro, Fresh Jersey, outside of New York. Lutnick was on his way to Paris to meet with the Arnault family who, as part of their dominion over LVMH, run the Cheval Blanc hotel group. The source close to Lutnick mentions he had long admired the hotels and pitched the idea of the Pierre joining the group.

Lutnick’s first stop, however, was in London. After his plane landed, he went to the Dorchester Collection’s eponymous hotel in Mayfair. Shortly after 9 a.m. on Thursday, Lutnick gathered with Cowdray, the Dorchester president, and Motasem Khashoggi, chairman and principal owner of the Khashoggi Holding Company. From the outside, it seemed like an unlikely trio. The Khashoggi family was mainly famous for its wealth, but that was decades ago, back when Adnan, Motasem’s relative, was one of the world’s leading arms dealers. Motasem is recognized internationally today not as a captain of Saudi industry but as the primary legal representative for the Khashoggi family following the brutal 2018 murder of his journalist cousin, Jamal, by the Saudi state.

The source close to Lutnick states he and Khashoggi “met and spoke about a variety of different things” in London, “including: Wouldn’t it be cool if the Pierre was a Dorchester Collection hotel.” Eight days after the London meeting, according to screenshots of WhatsApp messages reviewed by Vanity Fair, Khashoggi texted Lutnick to say that “Brunie”—Hassanal Bolkiah, the Sultan of Brunei, who owns the Dorchester Collection—had “directly” asked him to explore a deal for the Pierre.

It has been revealed that khashoggi then asked Lutnick if he could give one of his kids a summer internship and provided his phone number. (Vanity Fair verified that number, as well as the ones used by Lutnick and the elder Khashoggi in the chats.) Lutnick rapidly agreed to the father’s request. “We would be delighted to have your son join us,” he wrote. “I’m excited to invest in and build exciting companies together.”.

A week later, Khashoggi sent the chat his greetings “from rainy Frankfurt,” along with a draft letter of intent to the Pierre’s board to begin due diligence for a “potential acquisition of The Pierre Hotel” and a initiative to buy up “the remaining residential units.”.

Industry observers note that lutnick wrote back on Memorial Day. “I am flying to Europe this evening, Italy and France,” he texted. “I’ve made a few modifications to the letter of intent.” Promise a “complete renovation of the guest rooms, public areas, dining facilities, and amenities,” Lutnick suggested. And be sure to include target prices, both per room and for the whole thing.

Industry observers note that lutnick’s firm, Newmark, was supposed to be representing the sellers in this transaction. Yet here Lutnick was coaching potential buyers, in effect putting himself on both sides of the deal. It wasn’t a cardinal sin in the take-no-prisoners worlds of New York City real estate or MAGA politics, but it wasn’t strictly kosher either.

Recent findings suggest that lutnick was confirmed as commerce secretary in February 2025; he stepped down from his Newmark chairmanship then and transferred his Cantor Fitzgerald assets to his sons. Lutnick was still listed as a member of the Pierre’s “transaction committee” in March, when the board confirmed in a letter that Newmark was in negotiations with an unnamed “operator.” But not to worry, the board added: “No owner would be required to sell their unit or move to another one.”.

Residents scrambled to find out more. All they got back were rumors and whispers. One shareholder’s representative states he heard the chatter but “blew it off,” thinking that nervous residents were being “dramatic.” According to this representative, the attorneys at Holland & Knight, which had represented the Pierre for years, seemed to be in the dark as well. “You can’t sell a co-op. Never happening here,” one of those lawyers told the representative in this source’s recounting. (Holland & Knight declined to comment for this story.).

Recent findings suggest that in June 2025, the Fresh York Post reported that the Sultan of Brunei was in talks to buy the Pierre, along with Essam ­Khashoggi, an older relative of Motasem’s. The board, chaired by Michael Stern, didn’t provide many specifics in a July Zoom with shareholders but emphasized that a sale was in their best interest, according to multiple published accounts. Two months later, according to court filings, four co-op board members—the investor John Levin, former Coca-Cola CEO Douglas Daft, the lawyer and movie producer David G. Johnson, and former KB Home chief executive Bruce Karatz—approved a nonbinding term sheet to sell the Pierre.

Industry observers note that on September 16, at a gathering in the Cotillion Ballroom, Fried Frank lawyers broke the news to shareholders. Khashoggi Holding was the buyer, and the sultan’s Dorchester Collection would be the hotel’s managers. The price was astronomical, they mentioned, and would guarantee residents “at least three times the market value” for their apartments, Town & Country reported. But the transaction was different from the one discussed back in March. It was not just for the hotel and selected apartments. It was for the whole building, which meant the co-op owners had to vacate within 12 months. All of them.

BREAKFAST NEAR TIFFANY'S A young woman enjoys room service at the Pierre Hotel, 1943.

It has been revealed that an escrow account of $10 million, funded by the shareholders, would be “used for eviction proceedings” for any residents who refused to leave, according to a slideshow presentation delivered by the lawyers that day. And on that happy note, residents were encouraged to open the personalized envelopes that had been given to them at the door, one for each shareholder. Inside were estimates of how much they might get from a sale.

One person who was there claims it reminded him of a “game show,” and kind of an insulting one to the ultrarich in the room, for whom a few million dollars either way wouldn’t matter all that much. What was particularly galling, according to sources at the meeting, was the strategy for the building’s union employees. Many of them, they remarked, were like family—to each other and to the residents. The staff would have to begin to go even sooner. Before Khashoggi would be asked to put down a penny, Fried Frank noted in its presentation, the firm “will engage with the Hotel Gaming and Trades Union to negotiate terms for the termination of the Union Contract.”.

Employees at the Pierre tend to talk about their tenures in decades. “I only have 12 years here,” one staffer tells me without irony. Some ­workers have jobs that are so old-school, they’re not really jobs anywhere else: elevator drivers, telephone switchboard operators. Housekeeping staff wear black-and-white outfits that wouldn’t have been out of place in Audrey Hepburn’s day. “I’m very used to it,” this employee indicates, referring to the atmosphere at the Pierre. She means that as a positive.

Recent findings suggest that like many Pierre staffers, she’s an immigrant. A 2021 Fresh Yorker profile counted “49 languages” spoken by the staff, “including Cantonese, Creole, Danish, Farsi, Greek, Hindi, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian, Tagalog, Tamil, Tibetan, and Twi.” I spoke with employees who are originally from four different continents.

One was a man I’ll call Ray, who has put in more than a quarter century at the Pierre and would very much like to keep going, even if the severance deal written into his union contract is pretty sweet: Ray figures he could live off of it for a year. But then what? He’s still got kids in school. And at the other hotels in town, the competition for open positions is really intense; promotions come mostly from within. “The chances of getting hired [in his particular department] are almost zero,” Ray tells me. “So I wouldn’t want to get a buyout. I don’t want the hotel to be closed.” Just in case, he’s taken a part-time gig elsewhere.

In a recent development, “We’re not like these millionaires, billionaires, the Howard Lutnicks, the Tory Burches,” notes another Pierre employee. “Just working people, trying to protect their families.”.

The rumors about a sale have been around long enough, and loud enough, that they rattled the staffers I spoke to. Even a renovation could upend staffers’ lives: The remodeling at the Waldorf Astoria Hotel lasted eight years; more than 1,200 union workers were bought out of their contracts. “Most of us, we worry,” a housekeeper tells me.

It has been revealed that people move to the Pierre, in part, because of the staff. More than a few residents come to be taken care of, to be treated like five-star hotel guests in their own (second, or third) homes. Room service is available from 6:45 a.m. to 10:45 p.m. Housekeeping comes in seven days a week; the apartments I saw were immaculate in every way, part of the reason why maintenance costs can run tens of thousands of dollars per month. (“I haven’t made a bed since I was a kid,” notes one long-term resident.).

My mom for years talked about retiring to a place like this, not that she could’ve afforded it. For older people who can, it’s a way to have the help they need while still living on their own. You see a lot of women who’ve lost or split up with their rich husbands: Beriro, the philanthropist and animal-rights activist; Gale Hayman, the cofounder of Giorgio’s of Beverly Hills; Mimi Sternlicht, the social entrepreneur; Julie Opperman, the prolific author whose late husband started the Westlaw legal-research service.

You could, perhaps, confuse these women for pushovers, one Belle Vivier pump away from assisted living. At the July meeting, Dorchester and Khashoggi brought gifts for the shareholders: bright-red teddy bears. “For little old ladies to snuggle up to in their beds,” one resident laughs at lunch afterward. Then she grabbed my utensils to cut my food.

It has been revealed that these ladies were long past cuddly tchotchkes. Over time, several residents, most of them women and most of them over 65, had formed a loose coalition to learn what they could about the deal for the Pierre and figure ways to stop it. “It was a handful of older women,” the resident adds, “banging on the pipes, saying, ‘Listen up, people!’ ”.

Some of them, at least at first, were open to the idea of a sale; they had other homes, after all. But the cloak of secrecy around the deal infuriated them. So in the days leading up to the contentious reveal of the Khashoggi proposal in September 2025, Chiles and Beriro and others banded together with Hearst and Burch—relative youngsters—and lawyered up. “We became an informal little group: Tory and a bunch of widows,” one source with direct knowledge of the matter says, tongue a bit in cheek.

ABOVE BOARD Investor Austin Hearst is part of a group of Pierre residents who sued the co-op board to produce more information about the sale of the building.

In November 2025, the group sued the board to force it to produce more information about the sale, with Burch’s LLC as the lead plaintiff: how much the board really knew about the buyer; which third parties might benefit from it. Shortly after, Fried Frank lawyer Michael Keats criticized Burch in a letter to her attorney: “this [her tactics] comes across as completely unhinged.” On at least one occasion, according to a source familiar with the matter, a board member approached Burch to see if she might want to keep her apartment, even while Khashoggi bought everyone else’s. Burch refused. (“The Board never offered anyone any special consideration,” its president and chairman later wrote in a letter to shareholders.).

The suit was quickly dismissed when the board agreed to release some of the information.

A number of shareholders, meanwhile, had found other sources. Some of them enlisted, in the resident’s words, “spies” to ferret out what the sale truly entailed. In March, some shareholders, independently of the board, met with Taj CEO Puneet Chhatwal. People both for and against the deal pressed shareholders for how they were going to vote, like Capitol Hill whips.

In late July, a 41-page corporate intelligence dossier was delivered to my home in an unmarked envelope. Who commissioned it is unclear; the cover page is missing and the report is undated. But it provides a tough assessment of Khashoggi’s corporate expertise.

According to the report, none of Khashoggi Holding’s “eight subsidiaries and associated companies” operate in the “hospitality sector, and none appear to have any international presence or cross-border real estate capability.”.

The company’s “most prominent publicly reported investments to date,” it adds, are an approximately $37 million “pharmaceutical investment in Aleppo [Syria] and a cement factory partnership.” Other deals publicly linked to the company and to Motasem Khashoggi are substantial but of a similar size.

In recent years and especially in the second Trump administration, money from the Persian Gulf has backed an attempt to merge two of America’s iconic movie studios, completed a leveraged buyout of one of its biggest video game makers, and purchased some of Fresh York’s most prized office towers. Khashoggi’s deals, on the other hand, “are orders of magnitude smaller than the proposed Pierre Hotel acquisition,” notes the report, which claims that the company’s “registered capital” amounts to “approximately USD 266,000.”.

Perhaps it’s just a coincidence that during the July meeting in the Cotillion Ballroom, the Khashoggi and Dorchester representatives received question after question about how Motasem Khashoggi could possibly have the resources to buy the Pierre.

In a recent development, NEIGHBOR VS. NEIGHBOR Michael Eisner, the former Disney CEO, owns two apartments in the Pierre. He has been in favor of finding newly introduced ownership for the hotel.

“You mentioned the Khashoggi LLC is the buyer, but who is putting up the money behind the Khashoggi hedge fund?” one shareholder asked.

“There is no hedge fund. This is Mr. Khashoggi. This will be funded in all cash, and it is only him,” was the answer.

“We’re not going to leave you out there with an unfunded buyer,” added Patrick Dowd, a Fried Frank lawyer.

Recent findings suggest that the questions would prove prescient—but it would still be a couple of months before that became clear. In the meantime, the speculation and the finger-pointing continued—splitting neighbor from neighbor—as the possibility of a sale grew closer and residents had taken sides. “They run the hotel, in my opinion, very badly,” Eisner stated of Taj in that July Cotillion room meeting, adding that he “would not stay at this hotel” with them in charge.

Industry observers note that “Then sell your apartment. If you’re not happy here, leave,” Burch snapped, according to the same recording of the meeting. “You don’t have to force everyone else and fire 700 employees in the process.”.

“This is not your home,” Burch stated a moment later to a second shareholder, who tried to take Eisner’s side. The decay, the imperfections, they can be a hassle, for sure. But they’re also part of the throwback charm, a necessary side effect to living someplace with so much history. “I don’t need a shiny fresh hotel,” she added. “People actually love this place, as shabby as it may be.”.

Despite the rancor, the board and the Indian hotel operators tried to negotiate a way forward. Or at least a competitive offer to Khashoggi’s. After 10 months of talks, they finally came to what they thought was an agreement. Two agreements, actually: one to buy the hotel portion of the Pierre; the other to extend Taj’s lease, in exchange for a commitment to invest almost $400 million into the building. The idea was to give both options to shareholders, shortly after the Khashoggi presentation.

Then suddenly, with less than a week to go before the Cotillion room meeting, Taj withdrew. The bosses in Mumbai voted not to approve the transactions they had been negotiating.

GLOVES OFF Al Pacino’s blind tango in Scent of a Woman takes place the Pierre's Cotillion ballroom.

A letter from Chhatwal floating the idea of a $300 million investment was rejected out of hand by the co-op board. The heads of the board wrote to shareholders the next day: It’s Khashoggi or the status quo, no other choices.

Sources indicate that “Do you want to live here or do you not? Let’s not overcomplicate it,” Burch told the Cotillion room. “It’s going to be down to two options. You either stay with Taj. Or you leave, and then it becomes some fancy hotel that we have nothing to do with.”.

Industry observers note that about a month later, the board released the details of the Khashoggi deal in a proxy statement sent to residents. It was enormous—more than 200 pages—but perhaps not maximally persuasive. Departing residents were promised five free nights in a suite at one of Dorchester’s other high-end hotels, plus a set of perks. “Priority access to spa treatments” and free breakfast seemed unlikely to move the needle with a crowd accustomed to more elaborate pampering.

The following week, Khashoggi tried reaching out to shareholders directly. “I understand how personal this is,” he wrote. “I sincerely hope that you will welcome me and my family into the Pierre family.”.

This personal appeal did not work on those shareholders who were already dug in against the deal. “Where do you get off addressing me by my first name?” one emailed back to Khashoggi.

And with that, the window opened for voting the deal up or down.

The following day, the chairman and president of the Pierre’s co-op board wrote to residents that “a wire transfer instruction has been issued to transmit the $100,000,000 deposit.”.

According to recent reports, then something strange happened. Or rather, didn’t happen at all.

Khashoggi’s money didn’t show up.

Supporters of the sale were baffled. “We are told by all advisers involved that he’s, you know, intending to complete the transaction,” one of those supporters claims. “In my business experience, someone who is a wealthy individual who decides that they don’t want to do the deal,” this person adds, “they send you a nice letter or make a phone call and say, you know, ‘I’m very sorry, but circumstances have changed, and I’m moving on.’ ”.

It has been revealed that that call never came, though. In late September, the spokesperson for Khashoggi’s American holding tech giant told Vanity Fair that the firm “has the money required to close.”.

The board gave Khashoggi additional time to come up with the deposit. He failed to do so, and the sale was called off. All of that work, all of those millions spent, all of that rancor—turned out, it was for a lost cause. The Khashoggi deal was dead.

According to recent reports, in an interview with the Times, Khashoggi gave a dog-ate-my-homework excuse, blaming the bank for failing to send over his deposit. He gave a shout-out to his “good friend” Lutnick, who had led him to the Pierre deal in the first place and who had been poised to receive as much as a $100 million windfall from it. Then Khashoggi took a shot at the residents he was courting just a few weeks earlier. “They have their building, which I’m sure they know the condition of,” he said. “And I have my money. So I don’t know who’s the bigger loser here.”.

At the time of publication, an election for a new co-op board was set for December 1. At least one of the residents who opposed the Khashoggi sale is mulling a run; another of those shareholders is thinking about suing those folks who got them into this whole mess.

Industry observers note that but in theory, things at the Pierre will now largely go back to the way they were. Or at least they’ll continue along the same trajectory. Taj has more than 8 years left on its lease, plus an option to extend another 10. Together with the fresh board, they’ll figure out which of the renovations are a priority. Those costs will then be split with residents. The assessments could reach into the millions for each apartment. The disruptions from the construction could be considerable. No one will be forced to leave their homes in this crumbling old palace by the park. For now, the elevator drivers and switchboard operators get to stay.

Tech Report: I Tried Coros' Fresh 'Expedition-Focused' Smartwatch, and I'm Impressed

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (517 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, coros has unveiled the Vertix 4, an “expedition-focused” upgrade to the Vertix 2 and 2S.
  • In a recent development, this watch is being marketed as a major step up from the Vertix 2S, with an AMOLED display, a more refined design, satellite maps and, for the first time on a Coros watch, a built-in flashlight.
  • According to recent reports, that price does still undercut the latest Garmin Fenix 9 line-up, which starts at $999, though some rivals are cheaper still.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, coros has unveiled the Vertix 4, an “expedition-focused” upgrade to the Vertix 2 and 2S. Coros claims it pairs the brand's brightest display yet with long battery life, and after unboxing it myself, I can definitely say it has a more refined feel that could indeed suit the office as well as the summit.

In a recent development, this watch is being marketed as a major step up from the Vertix 2S, with an AMOLED display, a more refined design, satellite maps and, for the first time on a Coros watch, a built-in flashlight. The Vertix 4 will be available to buy starting on Black Friday, Nov. 27, but it won't exactly be at a discount: It costs $799, a $100 increase over the Vertix 2S.

According to recent reports, that price does still undercut the latest Garmin Fenix 9 line-up, which starts at $999, though some rivals are cheaper still. For instance, the Suunto Vertical 2 steel model costs $599, and the Garmin Fenix 8 is right now on sale for $749.99 at Amazon.

I've only just started testing the Vertix 4 and haven't even had enough time to get through its substantial battery life, but I can share some first impressions, particularly in how it compares with the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro that launched earlier this year.

Industry observers note that built-in flashlights have become a must-have feature on premium sports watches, and now the Vertix 4 is the first Coros watch to get one. Coros has departed from the usual layout, though. Garmin, Suunto and Amazfit put the light on top of the watch, but Coros places it on the side, between the digital dial and the back button.

According to recent reports, previous Vertix watches used a memory-in-pixel (MIP) display. MIP has advantages, most notably longer battery life, but I know I much prefer the vibrant display on AMOLED screens, like on the Vertix 4. It is the biggest visual change and a large part of why the watch looks more premium than its predecessors.

According to recent reports, coros claims up to 30 days in watch mode, or 10 days with the screen always on. It also quotes 48 hours of multi-band GPS tracking with the screen always on. I haven't had time to test these claims properly, so stay tuned.

Coros watches are high-quality sports watches, but don't expect to find all the little lifestyle features you've come to expect on a more traditional smartwatch:.

Music: It can store tracks, but only files you drag and drop onto the watch. It doesn't pair with streaming services.

Payments: There is no NFC payment support.

Watch faces: Customization is more limited than on rivals.

Recent findings suggest that on paper, the Vertix 4 looks like a significant upgrade: a better display, a more attractive design, a flashlight and satellite maps, at a price well below the Fenix 9 line-up. The $100 increase and cheaper alternatives like the Suunto Vertical 2 and discounted Fenix 8 will matter to some buyers, as will the limited smart features.

#211924. WoW: Forever’s Best Buffs Now Work As Intended

WoW: Forever’s Best Buffs Now Work As Intended

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1253 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that world of Warcraft: Forever players will now be able to get even more benefit from the game's strongest buffs, as developer Blizzard's latest hotfix has made World Buffs persist across loading screens as intended.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever players will now be able to get even more benefit from the game's strongest buffs, as developer Blizzard's latest hotfix has made World Buffs persist across loading screens as intended.
  • According to recent reports, world Buffs are powerful stat-boosting effects granted to players in a particular area for certain events.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that world of Warcraft: Forever players will now be able to get even more benefit from the game's strongest buffs, as developer Blizzard's latest hotfix has made World Buffs persist across loading screens as intended. World Buffs are powerful stat-boosting effects granted to players in a particular area for certain events. The most common World Buff players see is Warchief's Blessing on the Horde and the upcoming Might of Stormwind for the Alliance, which are granted to all players in Orgrimmar, Stormwind, and their surrounding low-level zones when players on their respective faction turn in a specific high-level quest. Now that players are reaching endgame and turning in the required quest, these buffs are popping off constantly. They grant a whopping 300 hit points, 15% melee haste, and 10 mana regen per five seconds for one hour. At lower levels, those are some serious stats, particularly the 300 HP. Unfortunately, players haven't been able to take full advantage of the buffs, as a bug was causing them to be lost when hitting a loading screen. That meant any time a group stepped into a dungeon or took a boat or zeppelin to a new location, their World Buffs would be removed. That has finally been fixed in the latest upgrade, so players can now enter dungeons with World Buffs to help maximize their damage and health. This should be particularly useful for doing dungeons at a slightly lower level than is intended, as the extra HP and melee haste is definitely noticable. Blizzard clarified in the patch notes that World Buffs will still be removed when entering raids, so players won't be able to stack as many World Buffs as possible before raid night, as was the case in previous versions of classic WoW. Other changes found in the patch notes include a fix for an Uldaman boss that players were exploiting to make fast gold. Another is a fix for "a few spells and abilities" that were causing more weapon-proc effects than intended, likely nerfing the DPS of whatever classes were taking advantage of the bug. You can read the full patch notes below. Blizzard recently outlined in the latest episode of the WoW: Forever podcast how it wants to get rid of the idea of "best-in-slot gear," as well as how the game's has overhauled old-school WoW's player-vs.-player systems. In other Forever news, the game's launch has seen more than 15 million characters created so far, with the highest weekly player numbers for WoW in 15 years. WoW: Forever November 23 Hotfix Patch Notes Classes Druid The 4-piece Feralheart set for Druids now correctly grants 4 Energy regeneration every 1 second for 5 seconds. Priest Mind Vision should no longer proc effects. Shadow Fixed an issue where Dark Inspiration was not granting the correct amount of %Spirit increase if Mind Flay was used to activate it. Fixed an issue where Chastise was not usable in Shadowform. Warlock Destruction Fixed an issue where Intensity was not working on Incinerate. Warrior Fixed an issue where players could have and use Mortal Strike from their spellbook, even without the Mortal Strike talent. This does not remove it from their spellbook but prevents it from being used without the talent point spent. Dungeons Uldaman The Obsidian Sentinel drops loot as intended. Items The Filcher’s Cowl no longer has a level requirement. Professions Cooking Boiled Clams, Clam Chowder, Goblin Deviled Clams, Giant Clam Scorcho, Undermine Clam Chowder, and Clam Linguine each now offer the correct Well Fed bonuses and have been recategorized in the recipe list under “Stamina Food”. Murloc Fin Soup has had its recovery and Well-Fed amounts increased to the next tier of food, bringing it closer to other food of that level. Engineering Fixed a bug that caused Goblin Engineer’s Renewal Gift and Gnome Engineer’s Renewal Gift to appear as broken, unusable question marks in the inventory. Fixed a bug that prevented “The Mortar: Reloaded” recipe from being learned upon learning the “Goblin Mortar” recipe. Leatherworking Fixed a bug that prevented Pattern: Centaur Hoofwarmers from being learnable. Quests Riverglades - Dunston Willis once again runs near the end of the escort “Dunston Checks Out.” Wetlands - After further study, the quest “For Further Study” now has rewards. Wetlands - The quest “Uncovering the Past” now rewards Ironforge reputation. Wetlands - The quest “Gleaning Our Future” now rewards Ironforge reputation. Races Fixed an issue where Wisp Form could be applied to players while they were alive. Spells Fixed an issue where a few spells and abilities were causing more weapon procs than intended. Fixed an issue where World Buffs would fall off when changing areas. They will still fall off when entering raid instances. Fixed an issue where Fengus’ Ferocity was granting twice as much Spell Power as intended. Fixed an issue where Darkmoon Faire buffs were granting twice as much power as intended.

World of Warcraft: Forever players will now be able to get even more benefit from the game's strongest buffs, as developer Blizzard's latest hotfix has made World Buffs persist across loading screens as intended.

According to recent reports, world Buffs are powerful stat-boosting effects granted to players in a particular area for certain events. The most common World Buff players see is Warchief's Blessing on the Horde and the new Might of Stormwind for the Alliance, which are granted to all players in Orgrimmar, Stormwind, and their surrounding low-level zones when players on their respective faction turn in a specific high-level quest.

Now that players are reaching endgame and turning in the required quest, these buffs are popping off constantly. They grant a whopping 300 hit points, 15% melee haste, and 10 mana regen per five seconds for one hour. At lower levels, those are some serious stats, particularly the 300 HP.

Industry observers note that unfortunately, players haven't been able to take full advantage of the buffs, as a bug was causing them to be lost when hitting a loading screen. That meant any time a group stepped into a dungeon or took a boat or zeppelin to a new location, their World Buffs would be removed.

That has finally been fixed in the latest patch, so players can now enter dungeons with World Buffs to help maximize their damage and health. This should be particularly useful for doing dungeons at a slightly lower level than is intended, as the extra HP and melee haste is definitely noticable.
